item.title: East Bay Food Halls + Markets
item.description: Rockridge Market Hall opened in 1987 on a simple idea: do all your food shopping under one roof. The East Bay took the hint and never looked back. Most peo
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Food Halls + Markets

Rockridge Market Hall opened in 1987 on a simple idea: do all your food shopping under one roof. The East Bay took the hint and never looked back. Most people run in for one vendor and bolt. The real move is grazing the whole floor. Seven halls and markets worth building a Saturday around.

Public Market Emeryville — 5959 Shellmound St, Emeryville. A sprawling international food hall next to Christie Park, sushi to tacos to BBQ to cocktails under one roof. Family friendly with easy parking. @publicmarketemeryville.

Swan's Market — 510 9th St, Oakland. A 1917 market building reborn as a food hall, anchored now by La Guerrera's Kitchen and Taylor's Sausage with a cluster of counters around them. Saturday morning staple in Old Oakland. @swansmarket.

Rockridge Market Hall — 5655 College Ave, Oakland. Opened in 1987 as a European style market, eight independent shops: cheese, produce, butcher, fish, bakery, wine, flowers, espresso. Curated like a Saturday market abroad. @markethallfoods.

Berkeley Bowl — 2020 Oregon St, Berkeley. Not technically a food hall, but the produce section is a Saturday destination on its own and the closest thing Berkeley has. Two locations, Oregon Street and West Berkeley on Heinz Ave. @berkeleybowl.

Old Oakland Farmers Market — 9th St at Broadway, Oakland. A Friday ringer, not a Saturday one, running more than 25 years and year round. One of the East Bay's most diverse and affordable markets, in the historic downtown blocks by Chinatown.

Berkeley Saturday Farmers Market — Center St at Martin Luther King Jr Way, Berkeley. Run by the Ecology Center since 1987 and the first market in the country to ban methyl bromide. Saturdays, year round, heavy on certified organic. @ecology.center.

Grand Lake Farmers Market — 746 Grand Ave, Oakland. Saturdays at Splash Pad Park by Lake Merritt, more than 40 farmers plus prepared food stalls down to dim sum. Walk the lake before or after. @aginstituteofmarin.

Seven Saturday grazes: Public Market Emeryville, Swan's Market, Rockridge Market Hall, Berkeley Bowl, Old Oakland (Fridays), Berkeley Saturday Farmers Market, Grand Lake. Which gets your morning, a food hall with a roof or a market under open sky?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Bakeries
item.description: La Farine has been making the same morning bun on College Ave since 1977, and the line still forms before the sign flips. Nine East Bay bakeries worth the
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Bakeries

La Farine has been making the same morning bun on College Ave since 1977, and the line still forms before the sign flips. Nine East Bay bakeries worth the calorie commitment.

La Farine — 6323 College Ave, Oakland. Making the morning bun since 1977. Newcomers order the croissant; the morning bun is what built the place. @lafarinebakery

Acme Bread — 1601 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. Founded 1983 by Steven Sullivan. Most people only know the Ferry Building stand; the Berkeley original is the source. @acmebreadcompany

Boichik Bagels — 3170 College Ave, Berkeley. The storefront opened in 2019 after years of pop-ups. New York water bagel done right, plus challah on Fridays most shoppers miss. @boichikbagels

Bake Sum — 3249 Grand Ave, Oakland. Pandemic pop-up to Nosh Award winner in five years. Asian-American viennoiserie, and the regulars line up Saturday mornings. @bakesumpastries

Fournee Bakery — 2912 Domingo Ave, Berkeley. Tucked behind the Claremont. Croissants and kouign amann that sell out by noon. Most people drive past on the way to the hotel. @fourneebakery

Sweet Adeline Bakeshop — 3350 Adeline St, Berkeley. In the Lorin District since 2008. Open Wednesday through Sunday, closing at 3pm; the locals know not to come Monday. @sweetadelinebakeshop

Starter Bakery — 5804 College Ave, Oakland. In the East Bay since 2010. Wholesale first, retail second, so the small storefront fools people into thinking it is closed. It is not. @starterbakery

Tao Yuen Pastry — 816 Franklin St, Oakland. A cash-only Chinatown bakery since the 1980s. BBQ pork buns and egg tarts under three dollars.

As Kneaded Bakery — 585 Victoria Ct, San Leandro. Artisan sourdough and breads that Food and Wine named among the country's best, now with a cafe in the San Leandro library. @askneadedbakery

Nine East Bay bakeries: La Farine, Acme, Boichik, Bake Sum, Fournee, Sweet Adeline, Starter, Tao Yuen, and As Kneaded in San Leandro. Which one has your standing weekend order?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Dim Sum
item.description: Peony in Oakland Chinatown pulled its dim sum carts years ago so every dish arrives hot off the kitchen line instead of circling the room. Six East Bay dim
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Dim Sum

Peony in Oakland Chinatown pulled its dim sum carts years ago so every dish arrives hot off the kitchen line instead of circling the room. Six East Bay dim sum spots worth the wait.

Peony Seafood — 388 9th St, 2nd floor, Pacific Renaissance Plaza, Oakland. A Cantonese banquet hall in Chinatown for over 20 years, open daily except Tuesday. Order off the sheet, not a cart. @peonyseafoodrestaurant

Ming's Tasty — 940 Webster St, Oakland. Crispy BBQ pork buns and shrimp dumplings. Most people walk past it for Peony; Ming's is where the regulars go on weekdays.

Tao Yuen Pastry — 816 Franklin St, Oakland. Order-at-the-counter dim sum to go, cash only. The cheapest serious dim sum in the East Bay, and most newcomers walk right past it.

East Ocean Seafood — 1713 Webster St, Alameda. The classic dim sum hall on the island. Most Oakland-side eaters never cross the tube; East Ocean is the reason to. @east_ocean_seafood_restaurant

Best Dim Sum and Pastry — 723 E 12th St, Oakland. A walk-up window with three-dollar pork buns. Most newcomers do not even register the storefront; locals stack ten buns to go on Sunday.

Big Dish Restaurant — 339 9th St, Oakland. A quiet Chinatown dim sum room locals send their parents to.

Six East Bay dim sum spots: Peony, Ming's Tasty, Tao Yuen, East Ocean, Best Dim Sum, and Big Dish. Which one gets your Sunday order?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Brunch
item.description: Mama's Royal Cafe has been running the same Oakland brunch since 1974, omelet of the month and a line out the door. Six East Bay brunch spots worth the wai
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Brunch

Mama's Royal Cafe has been running the same Oakland brunch since 1974, omelet of the month and a line out the door. Six East Bay brunch spots worth the wait.

The Wolf — 3853 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. Most default to dinner; the seasonal brunch menu is the better-kept secret. @thewolfoakland

Skillet'z Cafe — 37378 Niles Blvd, Fremont. A hometown favorite with omelets stuffed past the plate. First-timers order pancakes; the chicken-fried steak is what regulars wait for. @skilletz.cafe

Mama's Royal Cafe — 4012 Broadway, Oakland. Running since 1974; most order the omelet of the month, but the sourdough French toast is what people drive in for. @mamasroyalcafe

Bar Cesar — 4039 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. Most stick to mimosas; the Spanish-influenced brunch plates are the actual order. @cesarpiedmont

Lucy's Crepes — 39459 Fremont Blvd, Fremont. Savory and sweet specialty crepes; most order sweet, but the ham-and-Gruyere crepe is the local pick. @lucys_crepes

Hops and Beans Cafe — Fremont. A neighborhood staple for over twenty years, cash-friendly and unhurried.

Six for the weekend wait: The Wolf, Skillet'z, Mama's Royal, Bar Cesar, Lucy's Crepes, and Hops and Beans. What is your go-to brunch order?

item.title: East Bay Ice Cream and Desserts
item.description: Fentons has been scooping on Piedmont Ave since 1894, five generations in, and the black and tan sundae is the one they made famous. Six East Bay ice cream
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Ice Cream and Desserts

Fentons has been scooping on Piedmont Ave since 1894, five generations in, and the black and tan sundae is the one they made famous. Six East Bay ice cream and dessert stops worth the calories.

Fentons Creamery — 4226 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. Open since 1894. Newcomers order the sundae; the black and tan is the move. @fentons_creamery

Curbside Creamery — 482 49th St, Oakland, in Temescal Alley. A walk-up window most people think closed. It did not. Cones to go, open 12 to 9. @curbsidecreamery

Yogurt Park — 2433 Durant Ave, Berkeley. Soft-serve since 1977, cash only, portions that explain the line. Open till 11 most nights. @yogurt_park

Suju's Coffee and Tea — 4949 Stevenson Blvd, Fremont. Korean shaved ice and waffles, with weekend lines. Most come for coffee; the pat bingsu is the order.

Bun Appetit — 37120 Fremont Blvd, Fremont. Gourmet ube and pistachio donuts, and a soft-serve most locals do not know they do. Saturday is busy. @bunappetitdonuts

iScream — 1809 Fourth St, Berkeley. Made in small batches on Fourth Street, open daily till eight. The scoop to fold into a shopping afternoon.

Six for the sweet tooth: Fentons, Curbside, Yogurt Park, Suju's, Bun Appetit, and iScream. Which one is your standing order?

item.title: East Bay Sandwiches
item.description: Top Dog has grilled sausages on Durant since 1966, mustard self serve, cash only, and the line still forms at midnight. The East Bay counter sandwich is a
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Sandwiches

Top Dog has grilled sausages on Durant since 1966, mustard self serve, cash only, and the line still forms at midnight. The East Bay counter sandwich is a whole religion. Eight worth standing in line for.

Top Dog — 2534 Durant Ave, Berkeley. Since 1966, a grilled sausage on a soft roll, the condiments are yours to pile on and they still only take cash. The after midnight order near campus.

Saul's Delicatessen — 1475 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A proper Jewish deli on Shattuck since 1986, the matzo ball soup is the reflex but the pastrami Reuben is the one regulars guard. @sauls_delicatessen

Santoro's Italian Market and Deli — 475 Santa Clara Ave, Alameda. Mike and Heidi build supreme sandwiches to order on bread baked that morning and serve until it runs out. Call ahead, the lunch wait hits thirty minutes and they mean it. @santorositaliandeli

Kinder's Meats Deli BBQ — 1776 Arnold Industrial Way, Concord. A Contra Costa institution since 1946, three generations deep, and the Ball Tip sandwich is the one people cross the county for, tri tip carved straight off the smoker. @kindersbbq

Bakesale Betty — 5098 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. The fried chicken sandwich on a slaw piled bun that wraps a line around the block, handed to you off an ironing board out front.

Brothers Deli — 2700 Park Blvd, Oakland. A tidy Park Boulevard counter where the Italian sub is the move, real crunch in the bread and the meats stacked the way they should be.

Ike's Love and Sandwiches — 2172 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. Dirty Sauce and a stacked sandwich with a menu longer than the receipt, every one named after an inside joke.

Gregoire — 2109 Cedar St, Berkeley. French technique out of a takeout window since 2002, home of the crispy potato puffs and a sandwich that rewrites itself every season.

Eight for the line: Top Dog, Saul's, Santoro's, Kinder's, Bakesale Betty, Brothers, Ike's, and Gregoire. Which counter do you wait at?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Tea Houses
item.description: Asha Tea House travels to the source for its leaves and whisks the matcha to order. That's why students keep the Berkeley original packed. Five East Bay te
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Tea Houses

Asha Tea House travels to the source for its leaves and whisks the matcha to order. That's why students keep the Berkeley original packed. Five East Bay tea houses for a slow afternoon.

Asha Tea House — 2086 University Ave, Berkeley. Fairly-sourced leaves, matcha whisked to order, and a downtown room built for lingering. @ashateahouse

Far Leaves Tea — 2626 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. The one to get lost in a book, with an extensive menu and pu-erh by the pot. @far_leaves_tea

Teance — Fourth Street, Berkeley. A tasting bar where a proper oolong session takes longer than first-timers expect. @teance_fine_teas

Blue Willow Teaspot — 1200 Tenth St, Berkeley. More than 50 loose-leaf teas in a cozy neighborhood room with private nooks and a tea bar.

Malaya Tea Room — 920 Central Ave, Alameda. British-Malaysian afternoon tea, tropical and nostalgic, open Thursday through Sunday. @malayatearoom

Five East Bay tea houses: Asha, Far Leaves, Teance, Blue Willow, and Malaya in Alameda. Where do you go to slow down?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Cheese Counters
item.description: The Cheese Board Collective has been worker-owned on Shattuck since 1971, and the line at four is for the pizza, not the cheese. Six East Bay cheese counte
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Cheese Counters

The Cheese Board Collective has been worker-owned on Shattuck since 1971, and the line at four is for the pizza, not the cheese. Six East Bay cheese counters worth the gift.

The Cheese Board Collective — 1504 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. Worker-owned since 1971, with a cheese counter that will cut and sample anything you are weighing. @cheeseboardcoll

Market Hall Foods — 5655 College Ave, Oakland. The Rockridge cheese and charcuterie hall since 1987, home of the Pasta Shop counter and a Tuesday tasting most first-timers miss. @markethallfoods

Raxakoul Coffee and Cheese — 1578 Hopkins St, Berkeley. A family-run shop by Monterey Market pairing a serious cheese case with house-roasted coffee, leave with a wedge and a bag of beans. @raxakoulcoffeeandcheese

Berkeley Bowl — 2020 Oregon St, Berkeley. The cheese counter inside the legendary market, where the cutters will sample anything you are considering. @berkeleybowl

Farmstead Cheeses and Wines — 1650 Park St, Alameda. A gift-box counter in the Alameda Marketplace, cheese paired with a bottle from the back room. @farmsteadwines

Star Grocery — 3068 Claremont Ave, Berkeley. A neighborhood market with a Tomales Bay and Cowgirl Creamery counter that is walking-distance picnic gold.

Six East Bay cheese counters: the Cheese Board, Market Hall, Raxakoul, Berkeley Bowl, Farmstead in Alameda, and Star Grocery. Who are you building the board for?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.description: Ver Brugge has cut meat on College Ave since 1947, and the regulars still order the dry-aged ribeye a day ahead. Five East Bay butcher counters the Sunday-
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Butcher Shops

Ver Brugge has cut meat on College Ave since 1947, and the regulars still order the dry-aged ribeye a day ahead. Five East Bay butcher counters the Sunday-roast crowd trusts.

Ver Brugge Foods — 6321 College Ave, Oakland. On College Ave since 1947. The regulars order the dry-aged ribeye a day ahead. @verbruggefoods

Magnani's Poultry — 1576 Hopkins St, Berkeley. The Hopkins Street poultry specialist where locals reserve the heritage turkey by October.

Berkeley Bowl meat counter — 2020 Oregon St, Berkeley. Inside the legendary market since 1977, with a lamb selection most shoppers underrate. @berkeleybowl

The Local Butcher Shop — 1600 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. Whole-animal and locally sourced since 2011, with a Friday sandwich the regulars pre-order. @thelocalbutchershop

Baron's Quality Meats — 1650 Park St, Alameda. A family shop in the Alameda Marketplace where you build the burger blend at the counter. @baronsmeats

Five East Bay butchers: Ver Brugge, Magnani's, Berkeley Bowl, the Local Butcher Shop, and Baron's in Alameda. Who cuts your Sunday roast?

item.title: East Bay Seafood Markets
item.description: Tokyo Fish Market has run on San Pablo Ave since 1962, and the regulars time it for the morning sashimi-grade tuna. Five East Bay seafood markets worth a S
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Seafood Markets

Tokyo Fish Market has run on San Pablo Ave since 1962, and the regulars time it for the morning sashimi-grade tuna. Five East Bay seafood markets worth a Saturday.

Tokyo Fish Market — 1220 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. Since 1962. Time it for the morning tuna; closed Sundays. @tokyofishmarket

Berkeley Bowl seafood counter — 2020 Oregon St, Berkeley. The market's fish counter will butcher a whole fish for free, and most shoppers do not know to ask. @berkeleybowl

Monterey Fish Market — 1582 Hopkins St, Berkeley. Since 1979, the wholesale source half the town's chefs buy from, open to the public Tuesday through Saturday. @montereyfishmarket

99 Ranch Market — 3288 Pierce St, Richmond, in Pacific East Mall. Live tanks and a Dungeness selection that takes over the counter in November. @99ranchmarket

Sun Hop Fat — 501 E 12th St, Oakland, in Eastlake. A live-seafood floor where the regulars come for the Saturday shrimp.

Five East Bay fish markets: Tokyo Fish, Berkeley Bowl, Monterey Fish, 99 Ranch in Richmond, and Sun Hop Fat. Where do you buy for the home kitchen?

item.title: East Bay Coffee Roasters
item.description: Mr. Espresso has roasted over a wood fire in Oakland since 1978, one of the few oak-roasters left in the country. Seven East Bay coffee roasters worth a Sa
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Coffee Roasters

Mr. Espresso has roasted over a wood fire in Oakland since 1978, one of the few oak-roasters left in the country. Seven East Bay coffee roasters worth a Saturday detour.

Mr — Espresso. 696 3rd St roastery, cafe at 1120 Broadway, Oakland. Wood-fired roasting since 1978, the oak a difference you taste in the first sip.

Catahoula Coffee — 12472 San Pablo Ave, Richmond. An independent artisan roaster since 2007, with the roasting lab at the original location. @catahoulacoffee

Red Bay Coffee — 3206 Grand Ave, Oakland. Keba Konte's mission-driven, Black-owned roastery; the hibiscus iced is the regulars' order. @redbaycoffee

Timeless Coffee — 4252 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. An all-vegan roastery and bakery since 2012; the chocolate croissant is the sleeper. @timelesscoffee

Modern Coffee — 381 19th St, Oakland. A downtown shop sourcing from Stumptown and Counter Culture, with seasonal house syrups worth trying. @moderncoffee

Highwire Coffee — Rockridge Market Hall, 5615 College Ave, Oakland. Built into the Market Hall for a quick stop while you shop next door. @highwirecoffee

Cole Coffee — 6255 College Ave, Oakland. A Rockridge institution since 1991: cash only, no wifi, no laptops, and the line moves fast. @colecoffeeinc

Seven roasters: Mr. Espresso, Catahoula, Red Bay, Timeless, Modern, Highwire, and Cole. Which bean are you chasing right now?

If you're weighing a move near any of these, that walkability is a real factor, and it's the kind of neighborhood detail I cover street by street. I work across Alameda, Contra Costa, and San Joaquin counties.

item.title: East Bay Ramen
item.description: Three Chez Panisse alums have run a ramen counter on College Ave since 2013, rotating the menu weekly. The East Bay broth bench does not need the bridge. E
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Ramen

Three Chez Panisse alums have run a ramen counter on College Ave since 2013, rotating the menu weekly. The East Bay broth bench does not need the bridge. Eight ramen counters, Oakland to Berkeley.

Ramen Shop — 5812 College Ave, Oakland. A counter from three Chez Panisse alumni since 2013, weekly menu following Bay Area produce. @ramenshopoakland

Itani Ramen — 1736 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Chef Kyle Itani's izakaya-ramen spot, a seasonal bowl that changes monthly. @itaniramen

Mensho — 4258 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. The Oakland outpost of Tokyo's Mensho, farm-to-bowl, with the tori paitan as the flagship. @mensho_piedmont

Sobo Ramen — 2000 Milvia St, Berkeley. Named to SFGATE's top five Bay Area ramen, with tasting nights on the monthly calendar. @soboramenberkeley

Noka Ramen — 90 Franklin St, Oakland. Hakata-style tonkotsu and homemade noodles in Jack London Square, letting the broth do the talking. @nokaramensf

Ippudo — 2015 Kala Bagai Wy, Berkeley. The Berkeley outpost of the Japanese legend; the shiromaru and akamaru are the two orders. @ippudo

Tsuruya — 1926 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A focused, simplified menu in a smaller room, with a shorter line than the Telegraph corridor. @tsuruyaramen_berkeley

Marufuku Ramen — 4828 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Hakata-style tonkotsu from the SF original, the Temescal outpost open since 2023. @marufukuramenofficial

Eight East Bay bowls: Ramen Shop, Itani, Mensho, Sobo, Noka, Ippudo, Tsuruya, and Marufuku. Which is your standing order when the fog rolls in?

item.title: East Bay Ethiopian and Eritrean
item.description: North Oakland's Telegraph corridor has an Ethiopian row where Cafe Colucci has served injera for thirty-five years. Eight East Bay Ethiopian and Eritrean t
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Ethiopian and Eritrean

North Oakland's Telegraph corridor has an Ethiopian row where Cafe Colucci has served injera for thirty-five years. Eight East Bay Ethiopian and Eritrean tables worth the communal plate.

Cafe Colucci — 6427 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Thirty-five years in North Oakland, powered by Brundo spices, with a deep vegan and gluten-free menu. The doro wat is the order. @cafecolucci

Enssaro — 357-A Grand Ave, Oakland. A family-run spot where the sampler platter and the coffee ceremony are the full experience. @enssarooakland

Messob — 4301 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. Authentic East African cooking; the family platter with multiple wats is the move for a group. @messobethiopian

Barcote — 6430 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Michelin-recognized, open seven days; the tibs and fresh injera are the reason. @barcote_ethiopian

Lemat — 3212 Adeline St, Berkeley. Widely regarded as one of the best in the Bay, with dinner from 5pm. @lemat_ethiopian_restaurant

Shewhat — 6101 Shattuck Ave, Oakland. Eritrean and Ethiopian cooking on the Berkeley-Oakland line, open weekends from 4pm. @shewhatcafe

Addis — Oakland. Habesha Ethiopian and Eritrean cuisine, with a coffee ceremony on request and family platters across the full wat menu. @addisrestaurantoakland

Cafe Romanat — 462 Santa Clara Ave, Oakland. One of the oldest Ethiopian spots in the East Bay; the lentil dishes and tibs keep the regulars close. @cafe_romanat

Eight communal plates: Cafe Colucci, Enssaro, Messob, Barcote, Lemat, Shewhat, Addis, and Cafe Romanat. What is your standing order?

item.content:encoded:
East Bay Brunch, part two

Lois the Pie Queen has had fried chicken and grits going on 60th Street since 1949. Five more East Bay brunches worth the line, past the ones everyone already names.

Lois the Pie Queen — 851 60th St, Oakland. Open since 1949; the fried chicken breakfast and the creamiest grits in the East Bay. @loisthepiequeen_510

Mama's Royal Cafe — 4012 Broadway, Oakland. Running since 1974, cash-friendly and packed with regulars, with a 25-option omelette menu. @mamasroyalcafe

La Note — 2377 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A breath of Provence downtown; the lemon gingerbread pancakes are the named dish and the wait is real. @lanoterestaurant

Kitchen Story — 5422 College Ave, Oakland. Korean and international brunch, with kalbi morning tacos and Korean fried chicken and waffles. @kitchenstoryoakland

Ole's Waffle Shop — 1507 Park St, Alameda. A Park Street diner since 1927, waffles and pancakes off the griddle. @oleswaffleshop

Five more brunches: Lois the Pie Queen, Mama's Royal, La Note, Kitchen Story, and Ole's in Alameda. Which line do you actually wait in?

item.title: East Bay Craft Breweries
item.description: Drake's poured its first pints inside a restored 1922 Dodge dealership in Uptown, and the beer garden out back fills before the fog burns off. The Friday m
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Craft Breweries

Drake's poured its first pints inside a restored 1922 Dodge dealership in Uptown, and the beer garden out back fills before the fog burns off. The Friday move does not have to be a bridge and a wine bar. Nine East Bay breweries locals built the weekend around.

Drake's Dealership — 2325 Broadway, Oakland. A 1922 Dodge dealership turned beer garden, fire pits and wood fired pizza under the pergola, the barrel aged saison is the first sip order. @drakesdealership

East Brother Beer Co — 1001 Canal Blvd, Richmond. The lighthouse town brewery past the railroad tracks the judges keep handing medals to, clean lagers made the patient way.

Temescal Brewing — 4115 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. The pink beer garden on Telegraph, kids and dogs welcome to eight, crisp cans and a patio that fills by five. @temescalbrewing

Ghost Town Brewing — 1960 Adeline St, Oakland. The metal edged West Oakland original, the warehouse where the whole thing got loud in the first place.

Ghost Town Brewing, Laurel — 3506 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. The neighborhood second room up on MacArthur, same beer with a kitchen bolted on.

Original Pattern Brewing — 292 4th St, Oakland. Employee owned in Jack London, hazy IPAs that win the regional flights and a taproom bigger than it looks. @originalpattern

Faction Brewing — 2501 Monarch St, Alameda. On the old Naval Air Station with the city skyline across the water, twenty plus on draft and dogs on the patio. @factionbrewing

Fieldwork Brewing — 1160 Sixth St, Berkeley. A tap list that turns over weekly, order the flight first then commit, and do not skip the pretzel. @fieldworkbrewing

Canyon Club Brewery — 1558 Canyon Rd, Moraga. A Lamorinda brewpub with a dozen brewed onsite, food truck nights and weekend live music. @canyonclubbrewery

Nine for the weekend rotation: Drake's, East Brother, Temescal, Ghost Town twice, Original Pattern, Faction, Fieldwork, and Canyon Club. Which taproom is your first pour?

item.title: East Bay Livermore Valley Wineries
item.description: Livermore Valley sits 45 minutes from Oakland with more than 50 wineries on one AVA, and Wente has poured there since 1883, the oldest continuously family-
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Livermore Valley Wineries

Livermore Valley sits 45 minutes from Oakland with more than 50 wineries on one AVA, and Wente has poured there since 1883, the oldest continuously family-owned winery in California. Most Bay Area locals have never made the drive. Nine Livermore tasting rooms worth the Saturday.

Wente Vineyards — 5050 Arroyo Rd, Livermore. Family-owned and pouring since 1883, the oldest continuously operated family winery in California, with a 2026 concert season. @wentevineyards

Concannon Vineyard — 4590 Tesla Rd, Livermore. Established 1883, the same year as Wente; the Petite Sirah program built the Livermore reputation. @concannonvineyard

Murrieta's Well — 3005 Mines Rd, Livermore. A historic estate in the Wente family portfolio, with tastings on a stone patio and vineyard views in three directions. @murrietaswell

McGrail Vineyards — 5600 Greenville Rd, Livermore. A smaller family operation, Cabernet-forward, with a dog-friendly patio and the family often in the room. @mcgrail_vineyards

Cuda Ridge Wines — 2400 Arroyo Rd, Livermore. A Bordeaux-variety specialist; the Cab Franc and Petit Verdot are why regulars drive past the bigger names. @cudaridge

Las Positas Vineyards — 1828 Wetmore Rd, Livermore. An estate winery with a tasting room locals book for small events; the Chardonnay is the hot-day order. @laspositasvineyards

Retzlaff Estate Winery — 1356 S Livermore Ave, Livermore. An organic estate with picnic-friendly grounds and an 1885 farmhouse; they encourage you to bring lunch. @retzlaffvineyards

The Steven Kent Winery — 2245 S Vasco Rd, Livermore. A Cabernet-focused, single-vineyard program for the drinker who came for the reds.

Wood Family Vineyards — 2407 Research Dr, Livermore. A small-production family winery steps from Steven Kent, worth the stop on the same loop.

Nine Livermore tasting rooms: Wente, Concannon, Murrieta's Well, McGrail, Cuda Ridge, Las Positas, Retzlaff, Steven Kent, and Wood Family. Which one gets your first Saturday?

item.title: East Bay Indian
item.description: Fremont runs block after block of Indian dining along Fremont Boulevard and the Pacific Commons corridor, one of the densest South Asian food scenes in the
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Indian

Fremont runs block after block of Indian dining along Fremont Boulevard and the Pacific Commons corridor, one of the densest South Asian food scenes in the Bay. Most people default to the same two spots and miss the range. Nine East Bay Indian tables, Fremont to Berkeley, for the table that knows its dosa from its thali.

Anantara — 43852 Pacific Commons Blvd, Fremont. South Indian fine dining; the Hyderabadi biryani and the dosa platter are the orders, lunch and dinner with extended weekend hours. @anantararestaurant

Masala Republic — 4949 Stevenson Blvd, Fremont. Modern Indian in a sharing-plate format; the butter chicken and the truffle naan are the named orders. @masalarepublic.fremont

Delhi 6 — 39030 Argonaut Way, Fremont. North Indian classics done right; the lamb rogan josh and dal makhani are the standing picks, weekday lunch buffet. @delhi6fremont

House of Raha — 4137 Bay St, Fremont. Contemporary halal Indian; the kebab platter and lamb chops bring the date-night regulars back. @houseofrahaofficial

Mylapore — 39024 Paseo Padre Pkwy, Fremont. A Tamil Nadu kitchen and South Indian specialist; the masala dosa and Chettinad chicken are the first-timer orders. @mylaporeexpress

Kesari Chulha — 3400 Mowry Ave, Fremont. Mughlai and North Indian; the Hyderabadi dum biryani is the dish the family table fights over. @kesarichulha

Naga's Kitchen — 36472 Fremont Blvd, Fremont. Andhra-style heat, family-run; the gongura mutton and Andhra chicken curry are why regulars build the rotation around it. @_nagaskitchen_

Dera — 41035 Fremont Blvd, Fremont. Northern Indian and Pakistani halal, kebab-forward; the seekh kebab and mutton karahi are the sharing orders. @derafremont

Vik's Chaat — 2390 4th St, Berkeley. A Michelin-listed Berkeley institution serving regional chaat for over 30 years.

Nine Indian tables: Anantara, Masala Republic, Delhi 6, House of Raha, Mylapore, Kesari Chulha, Naga's, Dera, and Vik's Chaat in Berkeley. Which one is your standing order?

item.title: East Bay Thai
item.description: Jo's Modern Thai pulled a Michelin Bib Gourmand into the Laurel District, and it is one of several East Bay Thai kitchens the guide now sends people across
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Thai

Jo's Modern Thai pulled a Michelin Bib Gourmand into the Laurel District, and it is one of several East Bay Thai kitchens the guide now sends people across the bridge for. The bridge is optional. Ten East Bay Thai spots that earn the standing reservation.

Jo's Modern Thai — 3725 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. The Laurel District Bib Gourmand where the crispy rice salad and the massaman beef are why the reservation stays standing. @josmodernthai

Bird and Buffalo — 4659 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Isaan soul food out of Thailand's northeast, charred grilled meats and green papaya somtum, on the Michelin Guide since 2022. @birdandbuffalothai

Daughter Thai Kitchen — 6118 Medau Pl, Oakland. Southern Thai in Montclair from a Food Network Thai Takedown winner, order the crab curry and the southern style fried chicken. @daughterthaikitchen

Wawa Thai Food — 3009 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. A women owned Northern Thai kitchen in the Dimond grinding its own curry paste daily, the khao soi is the one to get. @wawathaifood

Farmhouse Kitchen Thai — 336 Water St, Oakland. A big patio and a full bar in Jack London, boat noodles and khao soi that run authentic while the cocktails hold their own. @thaifarmhouseoak

Khao Hom — 22545 Foothill Blvd, Hayward. Small, family run, regional Thai, the pad kra pao with crispy pork and the tom yum the regulars never skip. @khaohomhayward

Andaman Thai — 1560 Newell Ave, Walnut Creek. A neighborhood Thai with the kind of consistency that mints regulars, garlic prawns and panang the standing orders. @andaman_thai_restaurant

Praaw Thai — 1277 Gilman St, Berkeley. Bright and modern off Gilman, the som tum papaya salad and the basil fried rice with prawns are the lunch picks. @praawthai

Royal Siam — 512 Center St, Moraga. Three decades of Moraga regulars, the pad thai draws them in and the larb keeps them coming back.

Saneh Bangkok — 2634 Pleasant Hill Rd, Pleasant Hill. Bangkok street food the bigger rooms skip, the pork belly over sticky rice is the move.

Ten for the reservation: Jo's, Bird and Buffalo, Daughter, Wawa, Farmhouse, Khao Hom, Andaman, Praaw, Royal Siam, and Saneh Bangkok. What is your go to Thai dish?

item.title: East Bay Chocolate Makers
item.description: TCHO has run a bean-to-bar chocolate factory on San Pablo Ave since 2014, tours and all, and it is not the only real chocolate maker on this side of the Ba
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Chocolate Makers

TCHO has run a bean-to-bar chocolate factory on San Pablo Ave since 2014, tours and all, and it is not the only real chocolate maker on this side of the Bay. The dinner-party host knows where to buy; the new neighbor does not. Seven East Bay chocolate makers and shops worth knowing before gift season.

TCHO Chocolate — 3100 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. A bean-to-bar factory and tasting shop with reservation tours; the single-origin bars are the entry point. @tchochocolate

The Oakland Chocolate Company — 1552 Beach St, Oakland. A bean-to-bar maker working only with Jamaican cacao, a small shop open weekday mornings. @oaklandchocolateco2007

Coracao Confections — 1401 Marina Way S, Richmond. Raw, organic, plant-based bean-to-bar; the peanut butter cups and dark truffles are the move for vegan gift lists. @coracaochocolate

Chocolaterie — 1964 University Ave, Berkeley. The longtime Berkeley chocolatier once known as Chocolatier Blue, hand-finished truffles and bars.

Casa de Chocolates — 2629 Ashby Ave, Berkeley. A Latin American chocolate maker for truffles, barks, and custom gift boxes, artisan and unique.

The Chocolate Dragon — 5427 College Ave, Oakland. A Rockridge cafe locals love for house-made hot chocolate and a deep wall of craft bars. @chocolatedragoncafe

See's Candies — Multiple East Bay locations. The California classic since 1921; the rum nougat and the Bordeaux are the deep-cut picks for the in-laws' gift box. @seescandies

Seven for gift season: TCHO, the Oakland Chocolate Company, Coracao, Chocolaterie, Casa de Chocolates, the Chocolate Dragon, and See's. Which do you gift first?

item.title: East Bay Wine Bars
item.description: Ordinaire opened on Grand Ave in 2013 and helped turn Oakland into a natural-wine city that sommeliers now fly in for. The by-the-glass list is supposed to
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Wine Bars

Ordinaire opened on Grand Ave in 2013 and helped turn Oakland into a natural-wine city that sommeliers now fly in for. The by-the-glass list is supposed to change every week. Five East Bay wine bars where the pour rotates and you stay a while.

Bay Grape — 376 Grand Ave, Oakland. A tightly curated wine shop and bar in one; order three glasses to taste, then commit, and the cheese plate pairs itself. Closed Mondays. @baygrape

Ordinaire — 3354 Grand Ave, Oakland. The Grand Lake natural-wine bar and shop that put Oakland on the map; the small-glass format is the way in. @ordinaire_oakland

The Punchdown — 1737 Broadway, Oakland. A James Beard-nominated natural-wine bar downtown, list always changing, flights and half-pours on offer.

The Wine Mine — 5427 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A Temescal wine shop with bar service and a Saturday tasting where five wines run a dollar; the staff knows the small producers. @the_wine_mine

Snail Bar — 4935 Shattuck Ave, Oakland. An award-winning Temescal natural-wine bar with a seasonal small-plates menu that changes weekly. @snailbaroakland

Five for the rotating pour: Bay Grape, Ordinaire, the Punchdown, the Wine Mine, and Snail Bar. What spot do you bring out-of-town friends to?

item.title: East Bay Late-night Eats
item.description: Most of the East Bay goes dark at nine and the only thing open is a chain drive-thru. But Top Dog has slung linguica on Durant since 1966 and stays open pa
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Late-night Eats

Most of the East Bay goes dark at nine and the only thing open is a chain drive-thru. But Top Dog has slung linguica on Durant since 1966 and stays open past 2am. Six East Bay spots open past 10pm worth the trip.

Top Dog — 2534 Durant Ave, Berkeley. A hot-dog institution since 1966, open to 2am weekdays and 3am on weekends; the linguica with mustard, eaten standing up.

Tacos Sinaloa — 3132 E 12th St, Oakland. Open to 1am, where the al pastor and the mulitas are why the line never quits. @tacos_sinaloa_oakland

Kingfish Pub — 5227 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A dive in a 1920s former bait shop with Cal memorabilia, open to 2am on weekends with a real kitchen. @kingfishpub

Eli's Mile High Club — 3629 Martin Luther King Jr Way, Oakland. A dive bar and music venue with a proper kitchen running food till close, 2am on weekends. @elismilehighclub

June's Pizza — 2408 Mandela Pkwy, Oakland. A walk-ins-only New York slice spot, 4pm to midnight every day. @junes_pizza

MAMA Oakland — 388 Grand Ave, Oakland. Handmade-meatball Italian with a late-night sandwich window for the post-bar crowd.

Six for past-ten: Top Dog, Tacos Sinaloa, Kingfish, Eli's Mile High, June's Pizza, and MAMA. What is your post-midnight order?

item.title: East Bay Chilaquiles and Mexican Brunch
item.description: Sequoia Diner builds its chilaquiles on La Finca chips and house-made chorizo, and regulars order rojo or verde without opening the menu. The diner-counter
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Chilaquiles and Mexican Brunch

Sequoia Diner builds its chilaquiles on La Finca chips and house-made chorizo, and regulars order rojo or verde without opening the menu. The diner-counter version will always disappoint next to it. Seven East Bay spots for chilaquiles and Mexican brunch.

Cholita Linda — 4923 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Latin American comfort food where the baja fish taco draws the crowd, but the weekend chilaquiles and tortas are the locals' move. @cholita_linda

Dona — 3770 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. Dona Savitsky's reboot of her former Dona Tomas, a daily-changing seasonal Mexican brunch with chilaquiles and in-house pastries. @donaoakland

Nido's BackYard — 104 Oak St, Oakland. The Bay Area's first margarita garden, with green and black chilaquiles, one herbal-jalapeno with pulled chicken, one chile negro with grilled bavette. @nidosbackyard

Sequoia Diner — 3719 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. A husband-and-wife diner where the chilaquiles rojo with La Finca chips and the verde with house-made chorizo are the cult orders. @sequoia_diner

El Huarache Azteca — 3842 International Blvd, Oakland. Eva Saavedra's Mexico City-rooted spot; the huaraches are the house specialty but the red-or-green chilaquiles run a close second. @elhuaracheazteca_

Otaez — 3872 International Blvd, Oakland. A Fruitvale standby that still does the chilaquiles-with-steak-on-the-side combo most other places dropped. @otaez_oakland

Sofia's House — 3905 Broadway, Oakland. A family-owned newcomer that opened in January 2026 in the former Chimmelier space, brunch chilaquiles and omelettes. @sofias_house_oakland

Seven for the plate: Cholita Linda, Dona, Nido's BackYard, Sequoia Diner, El Huarache Azteca, Otaez, and Sofia's House. What is your standing brunch order?

item.content:encoded:
East Bay Eritrean Tables

Ethiopian food gets the East Bay attention, but Eritrean shares the injera and the coffee ceremony and holds its own identity, starting with Asmara since 1985. Five East Bay Eritrean tables.

Asmara Restaurant — 5020 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Oakland's first East African restaurant, family-run since 1985; the vegetarian combo and the kitfo are the orders.

Cafe Eritrea D'Afrique — 4069 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A North Oakland Eritrean cafe since 1986, breakfast plates, the coffee ceremony, and smaller plates for solo diners. @cafe_eritrea

Adulis — 346 Grand Ave, Oakland. A family-run Eritrean spot with the meat-and-veg combo plates and a weekend coffee ceremony.

Habesha — 6100 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A North Temescal Eritrean-Ethiopian kitchen with house-made injera daily and the vegetarian combo.

Red Sea — Berkeley. A longtime Eritrean and Ethiopian table with the combo platters and the coffee ceremony to close.

Five for the injera: Asmara, Cafe Eritrea D'Afrique, Adulis, Habesha, and Red Sea. What is your combo-plate order?

item.content:encoded:
East Bay Vietnamese Coffee Shops

If your morning cup has been the same chain pour for years, the East Bay has the phin filter and the sweetened condensed milk to reset it. Five East Bay Vietnamese coffee shops.

Cam Huong — 920 Webster St, Oakland. An Oakland Chinatown cafe where the ca phe sua da is the morning standard, banh mi on the side. @camhuongoakland

House of Phin — 1920 International Blvd, Oakland. A Vietnamese coffee specialist with phin-brewed ca phe sua da and signature drinks.

GA.RA — 2424 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley. A newer Berkeley Vietnamese coffee and food cafe, phin-brewed with black-sesame, ube, or pandan foam.

Binge Coffee House — Berkeley. A Berkeley Vietnamese cafe of ca phe sua da, banh mi, and pandan waffles.

Phin Vietnamese Coffee — 34460 Fremont Blvd, Fremont. A phin-filter specialty shop and the slow-drip ritual, out in Fremont.

item.content:encoded:
East Bay Halal Restaurants

Bismillah Halal Tandoori on Fremont Boulevard runs a deep Pakistani menu where the chicken biryani and the weekend haleem are the standing orders. When the chains get old, this is the fix, Oakland to Fremont. Five East Bay halal restaurants worth the standing order.

Halal Wings and More — 160 14th St, Oakland. A halal soul-food crossover downtown, the wings and the catfish basket the move.

Zaytoon — 1133 Solano Ave, Albany. A Lebanese halal spot for the lamb shawarma plate and the mixed grill. @zaytoon510

Truly Mediterranean — Berkeley. A Mediterranean halal counter for the falafel wrap and the chicken shawarma plate.

item.content:encoded:

Kiraku — Berkeley. A neighborhood izakaya of small plates and sake.

item.title: East Bay Burger Joints
item.description: There is a burger stand in Hayward that has flipped never frozen patties since 1958, sizes named Baby, Mama, and Papa, and it only fires the griddle Friday
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Burger Joints

There is a burger stand in Hayward that has flipped never frozen patties since 1958, sizes named Baby, Mama, and Papa, and it only fires the griddle Friday and Saturday. People plan the week around it. Nine East Bay burger joints worth the detour.

Val's Burgers — 2115 Kelly St, Hayward. The family griddle since 1958, Friday and Saturday only, 11 to 5, cash in hand. Order the Papa with a thick shake and get there before the bread runs out.

Nation's Giant Hamburgers — 317 Broadway, Oakland. A Bay Area lifer since 1952, where the burger comes giant and the fresh baked pie case is the reason regulars stay for a second plate.

Trueburger — 146 Grand Ave, Oakland. The order at the counter classic by the lake since 2010, burgers, fries, and a shake done exactly right, now with a second window on Broadway.

Barney's Gourmet Hamburgers — 4162 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. The Piedmont Ave staple for a build your own that lands almost too tall to bite, curly fries riding shotgun.

Smack Burgers — 160 W Juana Ave, San Leandro. The downtown San Leandro smash that built a following six figures deep, edges lacy and crisp, open seven days. @smackburgers

Park Burger — 4218 Park Blvd, Oakland. The Glenview corner for a smash style burger and a beer list pulled entirely from Oakland breweries.

Oh G Burger — 2062 Mountain Blvd, Oakland. Montclair Village's answer to the drive through, a real counter burger where the chain used to be the only game in the village.

Scolari's Good Eats — 1303 Park St, Alameda. An Alameda griddle burger with East Coast leanings, the patty that argues for the classic over the smash.

Smashville Burger — 8460 Edgewater Dr, Oakland. Smash patties out by Hegenberger, the reward you promise yourself on the airport run.

Nine for the detour: Val's, Nation's, Trueburger, Barney's, Smack, Park Burger, Oh G, Scolari's, and Smashville. Griddle classic or smash crust, where do you land?

item.description: Fremont's Little Kabul has the largest Afghan community in the United States, and one restaurant there has served kabobs and mantu for over 30 years. Most
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Afghan Restaurants

Fremont's Little Kabul has the largest Afghan community in the United States, and one restaurant there has served kabobs and mantu for over 30 years. Most East Bay diners have never made the drive. Five Fremont Afghan restaurants worth it.

DeAfghanan Cuisine — 37395 Fremont Blvd, Fremont. Afghan cooking for 30-plus years, kabobs, mantu, and bolani.

De Afghanan Kabob House — 37405 Fremont Blvd, Fremont. The kabob-house sibling a few doors down.

Afghan Awasana Kabob — 37012 Towers Way, Fremont. Charcoal kabobs and Afghan rice plates.

Authentic Afghan Kebab and Cuisine — 39965 Mission Blvd, Fremont. Kebabs and Afghan classics on Mission Blvd.

Fremont Kabob — Fremont. Voted a best Afghan restaurant in the Bay Area.

Five worth the drive: DeAfghanan, De Afghanan Kabob House, Afghan Awasana, Authentic Afghan, and Fremont Kabob. Have you been to Little Kabul?

item.content:encoded:
East Bay Barbecue and Smokehouses

A New York Times critic put an Alameda barbecue joint on the fifty-best-restaurants-in-America list in 2024. Fikscue is halal, and the brisket is crossed with Indonesian spice. Six East Bay barbecue joints.

Fikscue Craft BBQ — 1708 Park St, Alameda. Halal Texas brisket crossed with Indonesian flavor, on the New York Times fifty-best list in 2024. @fikscue

Everett and Jones Barbeque — 126 Broadway, Oakland. Founded in 1973 by Dorothy Everett on 700 dollars while raising nine kids, hickory-smoked and still family-run. @everettandjones

Saints Smokehouse — 218 13th St, Oakland. Brisket and ribs from Rashad Armstead, a Food Network Chopped champion. @saintssmokehouseoak

Smokin Woods BBQ — 4307 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Pitmaster James Woodard smokes over cherry and oak, Texas and Louisiana roots. @smokinwoodsbbq

Back Forty Texas BBQ — 100 Coggins Dr, Pleasant Hill. Family-owned since 1978, at the Nugget rib cook-off every year since 1991. @backforty_bbq

The Smoking Pig BBQ — 3340 Mowry Ave, Fremont. Angus beef brisket the specialty, smoking since 2014. @smokingpigbbq

Six for the smoke: Fikscue, Everett and Jones, Saints, Smokin Woods, Back Forty, and the Smoking Pig. Who runs your brisket order?

item.description: A few lunch hours a day. That is the whole window to get Bakesale Betty's buttermilk fried chicken sandwich, a cult order in Oakland since 2005 from a Chez
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Fried Chicken

A few lunch hours a day. That is the whole window to get Bakesale Betty's buttermilk fried chicken sandwich, a cult order in Oakland since 2005 from a Chez Panisse alum. Seven East Bay fried chicken spots.

Bakesale Betty — 5098 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. The buttermilk fried chicken sandwich with jalapeno slaw, a cult item since 2005, served only a few lunch hours a day. @bakesalebetty

World Famous HotBoys — 1601 San Pablo Ave, Oakland. Nashville hot chicken that began as a 2017 backyard pop-up, rated the top chicken sandwich in California. @worldfamoushotboys

Angeline's Louisiana Kitchen — 2261 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. New Orleans Creole cooking, the buttermilk fried chicken the signature. @angelineslouisianakitchen

Lois the Pie Queen — 851 60th St, Oakland. A soul-food landmark since 1951, now third generation, fried chicken and homemade pie. @loisthepiequeen_510

Home of Chicken and Waffles — 247 4th St, Oakland. The Jack London staple since 2004, chicken and waffles from a West Oakland native. @the_homeofchickenandwaffles

Noori Chicken — 366 Grand Ave, Oakland. Korean double-fried chicken in yangnyeom sauce, made fresh in Grand Lake. @noori_chicken_oakland

Pyeong Chang Tofu House — 4701 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A longtime Koreatown tofu house that also fries a mean soy-garlic Korean chicken. @pyeongchangtofu

Seven birds: Bakesale Betty, HotBoys, Angeline's, Lois the Pie Queen, Home of Chicken and Waffles, Noori, and Pyeong Chang. Whose chicken wins your Friday?

item.title: East Bay Wine Shops
item.description: The wine world flies to Berkeley for a plain storefront on San Pablo Avenue. Kermit Lynch has imported and sold wine there since 1972, and anyone can just
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Wine Shops

The wine world flies to Berkeley for a plain storefront on San Pablo Avenue. Kermit Lynch has imported and sold wine there since 1972, and anyone can just walk in. Six East Bay wine shops.

Kermit Lynch Wine Merchant — 1605 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. One of the world's great importers, the original walk-in shop open since 1972. @kermitlynchwine

Vintage Berkeley — 2113 Vine St, Berkeley. Small-production wine inside a decommissioned water-pumping station, a big selection under thirty dollars. @vbscwine

Paul Marcus Wines — 5655 College Ave, Oakland. The first shop to open in Rockridge Market Hall, European-focused, going strong since 1987. @paulmarcuswines

Bay Grape — 376 Grand Ave, Oakland. A small-production shop opened by two sommeliers on Grand Avenue. @baygrape

Farmstead Cheeses and Wines — 1650 Park St, Alameda. An Alameda Marketplace shop voted best wine and cheese store year after year, since 2003. @farmstead.wines

Wine Thieves — 3401 Mt Diablo Blvd, Lafayette. A bargain-minded wine and craft beer shop in Lafayette for over twenty-five years. @winethievesca

Six to uncork: Kermit Lynch, Vintage Berkeley, Paul Marcus, Bay Grape, Farmstead, and Wine Thieves. What is coming home for dinner?

item.title: East Bay Hot Pot Tables
item.description: Nobody has to cross a bridge to drop thin beef into a boiling pot. Fremont alone runs a hot pot cluster where one famous room keeps the broth going until t
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Hot Pot Tables

Nobody has to cross a bridge to drop thin beef into a boiling pot. Fremont alone runs a hot pot cluster where one famous room keeps the broth going until two in the morning, and the East Bay has seven more tables from Berkeley to Dublin. Eight pots, all on this side of the water.

Azure Hot Pot — 1700 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. All you can eat in North Berkeley with the pot boiling until 11 at night, so the Shattuck corridor finally has a table for it.

Boiling Point — 46807 Warm Springs Blvd, Fremont. Individual pots with house made broths, where the kimchi seafood and the stinky tofu are the orders regulars repeat. @boilingpointgroup

Haidilao — 43349 Boscell Rd, Fremont. The full theater of hot pot service at Pacific Commons, hand pulled noodles at the table and broth running until two in the morning every night.

Mumu Hot Pot — 5699 Bay St, Emeryville. Individual pots and a build your own sauce bar at Bay Street, ordered a la carte, with a weekend wait that tells you why.

Hotpot Nation — 3288 Pierce St, Richmond. Inside Pacific East Mall under the same roof as 99 Ranch, broth going until 11 most nights, so dinner and the grocery run happen in one trip.

Shabuya — 2025 Diamond Blvd, Concord. All you can eat shabu with a personal pot at every seat, open to 10 on weeknights and 11 on the weekend, Central Contra Costa covered.

Shabu King — 3872 Fallon Rd, Dublin. The Tri Valley answer, all you can eat with your own pot and a long list of broths, so eastern Alameda County stays on this side of the bridge.

Hungry Cow — 40470 Albrae St, Fremont. Korean barbecue and shabu shabu under one roof near the Auto Mall, a build your own sauce bar and a grill the staff swap the second you need it. @myhungrycow

Eight pots, no bridge toll: Azure in Berkeley, Boiling Point, Haidilao and Hungry Cow in Fremont, Mumu in Emeryville, Hotpot Nation in Richmond, Shabuya in Concord, and Shabu King in Dublin. Which broth gets your winter Friday?

item.title: East Bay Dumplings and Soup Dumplings
item.description: The soup dumpling king of Oakland Chinatown closed, and everyone assumed you had to cross a bridge for a proper xiao long bao again. Wrong. Rockridge to Ne
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Dumplings and Soup Dumplings

The soup dumpling king of Oakland Chinatown closed, and everyone assumed you had to cross a bridge for a proper xiao long bao again. Wrong. Rockridge to Newark to Dublin, the East Bay quietly rebuilt its dumpling bench. Eight spots for the broth filled bite.

United Dumplings — 6247 College Ave, Oakland. A Rockridge dumpling house since 2023, creative fillings like Korean barbecue and chicken mushroom truffle alongside the classics. @uniteddumplings

Din Ding Dumpling House — 3768 Capitol Ave, Fremont. A family dumpling house whose thin skin xiao long bao is the order, rebuilt on Capitol Ave after a fire. @dindingdumplingbayarea

88 Bao Bao — 3880 Fallon Rd, Dublin. A Tri Valley spot since 2018 built around the soup dumpling, delicate skins that burst with broth. @88baobao_official

Qi Dumpling Lounge — 3300 Grand Ave, Oakland. Soup dumplings, pork bun sliders, and dragon dumplings in a Grand Lake dining room, weekends run late.

Dumpling Hours — 3331 Lakeshore Ave, Oakland. From the Dumpling Home team, broth packed xiao long bao served steamed, boiled, or pan fried by Lake Merritt.

HuangCheng Potsticker — 907 Washington St, Oakland. Inside Swan's Market in Chinatown since 2024, pork or shrimp dumplings boiled or pan fried from the Huangcheng noodle team.

Dumpling and Noodle House — 1768 Willow Pass Rd, Concord. Homemade pan fried pork buns and hand made dumplings in Concord, seven days a week.

Shanghai Bistro — 39169 Cedar Blvd, Newark. A Shanghai style room in Newark for xiao long bao and pan fried sheng jian bao, closed Wednesdays.

Eight for the broth filled bite, Oakland to Newark: United Dumplings, Qi, Dumpling Hours and HuangCheng in Oakland, Din Ding in Fremont, 88 Bao Bao in Dublin, Dumpling and Noodle House in Concord, and Shanghai Bistro in Newark. Which skin do you pinch first?

item.description: Lois the Pie Queen has had fried chicken and grits going on 60th Street since 1949. Ten East Bay brunches worth the line, from that counter to a 1927 Alame
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Brunch

Lois the Pie Queen has had fried chicken and grits going on 60th Street since 1949. Ten East Bay brunches worth the line, from that counter to a 1927 Alameda waffle house.

Lois the Pie Queen — 851 60th St, Oakland. Open since 1949, the fried chicken breakfast and the creamiest grits in the East Bay. @loisthepiequeen_510

Mama's Royal Cafe — 4012 Broadway, Oakland. Running since 1974, a 25 option omelette menu and the sourdough French toast people drive in for. @mamasroyalcafe

Ole's Waffle Shop — 1507 Park St, Alameda. A Park Street diner since 1927, waffles and pancakes off the griddle. @oleswaffleshop

The Wolf — 3853 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. Most default to dinner, the seasonal brunch menu is the better kept secret. @thewolfoakland

Skillet'z Cafe — 37378 Niles Blvd, Fremont. A hometown favorite with omelets stuffed past the plate, the chicken fried steak is what regulars wait for. @skilletz.cafe

Bar Cesar — 4039 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. Most stick to mimosas, the Spanish influenced brunch plates are the actual order. @cesarpiedmont

La Note — 2377 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A breath of Provence downtown, the lemon gingerbread pancakes are the named dish and the wait is real. @lanoterestaurant

Kitchen Story — 5422 College Ave, Oakland. Korean and international brunch, with kalbi morning tacos and Korean fried chicken and waffles. @kitchenstoryoakland

Lucy's Crepes — 39459 Fremont Blvd, Fremont. Savory and sweet specialty crepes, the ham and Gruyere is the local pick. @lucys_crepes

Hops and Beans Cafe — Fremont. A neighborhood staple for overstuffed omelets and strong coffee.

Ten worth the line: Lois the Pie Queen, Mama's Royal, Ole's, the Wolf, Skillet'z, Bar Cesar, La Note, Kitchen Story, Lucy's, and Hops and Beans. Which table gets your Sunday?

item.description: Oakland has a banh mi row on International Boulevard where the shops bake their own crackly rolls every morning and charge you six dollars. Most people dri
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Banh Mi Counters

Oakland has a banh mi row on International Boulevard where the shops bake their own crackly rolls every morning and charge you six dollars. Most people drive to the same chain. Eight Vietnamese sandwich counters, Oakland to Stockton, where the bread is the whole argument.

Banh Mi Ba Le — 1909 International Blvd, Oakland. Cash only on International Blvd, two dozen sandwich varieties on airy crackly rolls, closed Mondays.

Cam Huong — 702 International Blvd, Oakland. A Little Saigon institution that bakes its own bread daily, crusty rolls and ample pickles, open seven days.

Nom Nom Banh Mi — 2491 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley. Feeding Berkeley since 2019, daily pickled carrot and daikon on bread baked fresh each morning.

Mom's Bun Mi — 1400 14th Ave, Oakland. A Vietnamese sandwich specialist near the lake, the grilled chicken banh mi is the order and some items sell out by afternoon.

Banh Mi Ba Le — 10174 San Pablo Ave, El Cerrito. Run by the niece of the Oakland Ba Le, especially toasty bread and a ham and head cheese regulars swear by.

Spicy Joi — 1687 Willow Pass Rd, Concord. A Lao and Vietnamese street food spot in Concord that grew from a sausage booth, banh mi and more since 2022. @spicyjoibanhmixlaostreetfood

Huong Lan Sandwiches — 7555 Pacific Ave, Stockton. A Stockton sandwich counter, the special combo and the beef teriyaki are the sellers, quick pickup.

Banh Mi and Roll — 347 E Weber Ave, Stockton. A downtown Stockton Vietnamese sandwich spot for the everyday banh mi.

Eight rolls, Oakland to Stockton: Banh Mi Ba Le, Cam Huong and Mom's in Oakland, Nom Nom in Berkeley, the other Ba Le in El Cerrito, Spicy Joi in Concord, and Huong Lan and Banh Mi and Roll in Stockton. Where is your six dollar lunch?

item.title: East Bay Vietnamese Coffee Shops
item.description: GA.RA on Telegraph pours robusta the Nguyen siblings grow on their own family farm in Vietnam, then roast in small batches. It started as a garage pop up,
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Vietnamese Coffee Shops

GA.RA on Telegraph pours robusta the Nguyen siblings grow on their own family farm in Vietnam, then roast in small batches. It started as a garage pop up, ga ra is Vietnamese for garage. Now the East Bay has real phin coffee. Six Vietnamese cafes worth the drive.

GA.RA — 2424 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley. Family farmed robusta, ca phe sua da, plus phin drip with black sesame, ube, and pandan foam. @cafegara

House of Phin — 1920 International Blvd, Oakland. Every cup hand brewed through the phin filter with deep roast robusta, the slow drip method. @houseofphin_

Phin Cafe — 34460 Fremont Blvd, Fremont. The egg coffee is the order, custard foam over strong coffee, plus pandan and durian versions. @phincafeus

Binge Coffee House — 2199 Bancroft Way, Berkeley. A compact spot near campus, Vietnamese coffee alongside a matcha lab and banh mi. @bingecoffeehouse

Lac Coffee — 39658 Cedar Blvd, Newark. Vietnamese owned, beans from Vietnam and matcha from Japan, a calm ca phe sua da stop. @laccoffee.ca

Cafe Da Huong — 605 E 12th St, Oakland. A no frills Little Saigon mainstay, cash only, the iced Vietnamese coffee strong and sweet.

Six for the phin, Berkeley to Newark: GA.RA, House of Phin, Phin Cafe, Binge, Lac Coffee, and Cafe Da Huong. Which ca phe sua da is your regular?

item.title: East Bay Pizza
item.description: The Cheese Board in Berkeley bakes a single pizza flavor a day, no menu, no choices, and the line still runs down Shattuck before the doors open. The East
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Pizza

The Cheese Board in Berkeley bakes a single pizza flavor a day, no menu, no choices, and the line still runs down Shattuck before the doors open. The East Bay takes its pizza personally. Eight pies worth planning a night around.

The Cheese Board Collective — 1512 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. One vegetarian pizza a day, decided that morning, sold by the slice while a jazz trio plays in the corner. Check the board, get in line, thank me later.

Zachary's Chicago Pizza — 5801 College Ave, Oakland. The stuffed deep dish that has run Rockridge since 1983, a molten pie you order before you sit because it bakes for half an hour. Worth every minute.

Pizzaiolo — 5008 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. The wood fired Temescal room where the crust chars blistered and the toppings change with the market. Book ahead for the weekend and sit at the counter.

Emilia's Pizzeria — 2995 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A tiny counter turning out New York style slices so good it sells out and closes early, cash and patience required. Thin, chewy, foldable, the real East Coast thing.

Little Star Pizza — 1181 Solano Ave, Albany. Chicago deep dish with a cornmeal crust plus a thin crust for the table that cannot agree. The deep dish is the reason to cross into Albany. @littlestarsolano

Arizmendi Bakery — 3265 Lakeshore Ave, Oakland. The worker owned co-op that bakes one gourmet pizza a day, corn and cheese one morning, roasted squash the next. Grab a slice and a scone. @arizmendilakeshore

June's Pizza — 2408 Mandela Pkwy, Oakland. The West Oakland spot that came back, sourdough crust and a short rotating list, small batch and worth the wait. Watch for the day it fires the oven.

Lo Coco's — 4270 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. Family run Sicilian since 1982, the thin crust with the garlicky red sauce your nonna wishes she made. BYO wine and settle in. @lococospiedmont

Eight pies: Cheese Board, Zachary's, Pizzaiolo, Emilia's, Little Star, Arizmendi, June's, and Lo Coco's. Which crust wins your Friday?

item.title: East Bay Italian Restaurants
item.description: At Belotti in Rockridge they roll and cut the pasta by hand in the front window, and by the time it reaches your table it has been made twice, once for sho
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Italian Restaurants

At Belotti in Rockridge they roll and cut the pasta by hand in the front window, and by the time it reaches your table it has been made twice, once for show and once for real. Seven East Bay Italian rooms that skip the red checkered cliche.

Belotti Ristorante e Bottega — 5403 College Ave, Oakland. Hand rolled pasta from the bottega up front, tajarin with thirty egg yolks and a ragu that took all day. Sit at the counter and watch. @belottirb

Bellanico — 4238 Park Blvd, Oakland. The Glenview room named for a Verdi opera, seasonal Italian and a wine list built for lingering on a Tuesday. Neighborhood dinner done right. @bellanicorestaurant_oakland

Via del Corso — 1788 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. Walk in and you could be in a Florence trattoria, house made pastas and a Tuscan hand in the kitchen. North Berkeley's quiet gem. @viadelcorsoberkeley

Oliveto — 5655 College Ave, Oakland. The Rockridge institution since 1986, seasonal whole animal dinners and handmade pasta upstairs, a market cafe down below. The truffle dinners sell out for a reason.

Marzano — 4214 Park Blvd, Oakland. A Dimond District dining bar around a wood fired oven, Neapolitan pizza and Southern Italian plates under low light. The neighborhood date night that always delivers.

Montecatini Ristorante — 1528 Civic Dr, Walnut Creek. Old school white tablecloth Italian, veal, osso buco, and pastas in a hushed room that feels like Sunday dinner at a big family's house.

Trabocco — 2213 South Shore Center, Alameda. Coastal Italian on the island, fresh pasta and cocktails with a patio when the fog lifts. Named for the fishing piers of Abruzzo. @trabocco_alameda

Seven rooms, Rockridge to Walnut Creek: Belotti, Bellanico, Via del Corso, Oliveto, Marzano, Montecatini, and Trabocco. Where is your anniversary table?

item.title: East Bay Classic Diners
item.description: Ole's Waffle Shop has flipped waffles on the same Park Street corner in Alameda since 1927, same booths, same neon, same short stack. Six East Bay diners w
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Classic Diners

Ole's Waffle Shop has flipped waffles on the same Park Street corner in Alameda since 1927, same booths, same neon, same short stack. Six East Bay diners where the coffee is bottomless and nobody rushes you out.

Ole's Waffle Shop — 1507 Park St, Alameda. Waffles off the old irons, hash browns crisped on a flat top older than your grandparents, and a counter that still spins. Order the waffle, split an omelette, stay for the third coffee.

Oceanview Diner — 1807 Fourth St, Berkeley. The Fourth Street institution that spent forty years as Bette's, still packing the weekend line for the souffle pancake and the scramble. Put your name down and go browse the block.

Mama's Royal Cafe — 4012 Broadway, Oakland. A shabby chic Oakland breakfast temple since the seventies, wild omelettes, vintage everything, and the waitstaff sass that comes free. Cash is king, patience required.

Rudy's Can't Fail Cafe — 4081 Hollis St, Emeryville. The Emeryville punk rock diner, milkshakes and tater tots under a wall of kitsch, breakfast served late into the night. Loud, cheap, and open when you need it. @rudyscantfail

Rick and Ann's — 2922 Domingo Ave, Berkeley. The comfort breakfast across from the Claremont, red flannel hash and pancakes people drive in from two counties for. The weekend wait is real and worth it.

Fat Apple's — 1346 Martin Luther King Jr Way, Berkeley. The family standby for olallieberry pie and a proper breakfast, unfussy and generous, the booth you slide into with the kids.

Six for the bottomless cup: Ole's, Oceanview, Mama's Royal, Rudy's, Rick and Ann's, and Fat Apple's. Which booth is your Sunday?

item.title: East Bay Urban Wineries and Tasting Rooms
item.description: You can taste through more wineries on a single West Berkeley block than on a whole day trip to Napa, all natural wine, all poured in warehouses off Gilman
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Urban Wineries and Tasting Rooms

You can taste through more wineries on a single West Berkeley block than on a whole day trip to Napa, all natural wine, all poured in warehouses off Gilman. Six East Bay tasting rooms with zero drive to wine country.

Broc Cellars — 1300 Fifth St, Berkeley. The anchor of the West Berkeley wine block, low intervention California wine poured in a warehouse room, the zinfandel and the chilled reds a local favorite. Saturdays get social.

Donkey and Goat — 1340 Fifth St, Berkeley. A husband and wife natural winery a door down, skin contact whites and old vine grenache made by hand since 2004. Ask what is open and let them pour.

Hammerling Wines — Fifth Street, Berkeley. A newer name on the same natural wine block, small lots and a tasting bar built for lingering. Part of the Saturday wine walk.

Vinca Minor — West Berkeley wine block, Berkeley. Tiny production natural wine poured in a stripped down warehouse space, the kind of spot where the winemaker is often the one pouring.

Urban Legend Cellars — 1951 Monarch St, Alameda. Out on Alameda Point's Spirits Alley, Italian and Iberian varieties you rarely see, barbera to tannat, in a hangar with a patio. Open Friday to Sunday.

Dashe Cellars — 1951 Monarch St, Alameda. A family winery in an old airplane hangar, dry creek zinfandel since 1996 and a city view patio, the tanks right there behind the bar. Watch the wine get made.

Six pours, no drive to Napa: Broc, Donkey and Goat, Hammerling, Vinca Minor, Urban Legend, and Dashe. Which tasting room first?

item.title: East Bay Fine Dining and Special Occasion Tables
item.description: There is a door on Piedmont Avenue with no sign, and behind it is the only kitchen in the East Bay holding a pair of Michelin stars. Six East Bay tables fo
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Fine Dining and Special Occasion Tables

There is a door on Piedmont Avenue with no sign, and behind it is the only kitchen in the East Bay holding a pair of Michelin stars. Six East Bay tables for the night that matters.

Commis — 3859 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. The East Bay's only two star Michelin room, a long tasting menu at a narrow counter, precise and quiet and worth the splurge. Book weeks out and give it the whole evening.

Chez Panisse — 1517 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. Alice Waters' 1971 birthplace of California cuisine, the fixed menu downstairs, the a la carte cafe up top, still the most influential restaurant in the state. The origin story you can eat.

Wood Tavern — 6317 College Ave, Oakland. The Rockridge standby that nails the special occasion without the stiffness, a bustling room, a great bar, and a menu that never misses. The reliable yes.

A Cote — 5478 College Ave, Oakland. Small plates and a legendary back patio under the heat lamps, the mussels with pastis and a deep wine list. Date night that has worked for twenty years.

Comal — 2020 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. Upscale Oaxacan in a soaring downtown room with a hidden back patio and fire pit, mezcal cocktails and wood grilled everything. Group dinner headquarters.

iyasare — 1830 Fourth St, Berkeley. Cal Japanese on Fourth Street with a heated patio, seasonal small plates and sushi that punches at city prices. The understated splurge.

Six for the night that matters: Commis, Chez Panisse, Wood Tavern, A Cote, Comal, and iyasare. What are you celebrating?

item.title: East Bay Chinese Noodle Houses
item.description: At Shan Dong in Oakland Chinatown they pull the wheat noodles by hand to order, and the line for the pork dumplings has run out the door for thirty years.
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Chinese Noodle Houses

At Shan Dong in Oakland Chinatown they pull the wheat noodles by hand to order, and the line for the pork dumplings has run out the door for thirty years. Five East Bay noodle houses worth the wait.

Shan Dong — 328 10th St, Oakland. Hand pulled noodles and pan fried dumplings in the heart of Chinatown, the garlic noodles and the potstickers the reason the line never quits. Go early or go patient.

Classic Guilin Rice Noodles — 188 10th St, Oakland. A tiny counter doing one thing right, Guilin style rice noodles in a deep broth with the pickled sides, cheap, fast, and exactly what you wanted.

Gum Kuo — 388 9th St, Oakland. The Chinatown congee and noodle house locals lean on, silky rice porridge and wonton noodle soup, closed Wednesdays so plan around it. Comfort in a bowl.

Shooting Star Cafe — 1068 Webster St, Oakland. An all day Hong Kong style cafe, clay pot rice and noodle soups and milk tea, the kind of menu with something for every mood.

Huangcheng Noodle House — 8th Street, Oakland Chinatown. Northern Chinese hand cut noodles and hand pulled bowls, chewy and blistered with cumin lamb or tomato and egg. The newer Chinatown noodle fix.

Five for the slurp: Shan Dong, Classic Guilin, Gum Kuo, Shooting Star, and Huangcheng. Which bowl is your regular?

item.title: East Bay Waterfront Dining
item.description: Quinn's Lighthouse in Oakland is a real 1903 lighthouse that was floated down the estuary and turned into a pub, upstairs deck and all. Five East Bay table
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Waterfront Dining

Quinn's Lighthouse in Oakland is a real 1903 lighthouse that was floated down the estuary and turned into a pub, upstairs deck and all. Five East Bay tables right on the water.

Quinn's Lighthouse — Embarcadero Cove, Oakland. A restored 1903 lighthouse turned pub and restaurant, a cozy downstairs bar and an upstairs deck over the estuary. Order a mai tai and watch the boats.

Skates on the Bay — 100 Seawall Dr, Berkeley. The Berkeley Marina landmark where you walk out over the water to get in, floor to ceiling bay views and the Golden Gate straight ahead. Sunset with the crab cakes.

Lake Chalet — 1520 Lakeside Dr, Oakland. A grand boathouse on Lake Merritt with a long bar and a dock patio, gondolas drifting past at golden hour. Happy hour on the water in the middle of the city.

Eve's Waterfront — Embarcadero West, Oakland. A modern room on the Jack London waterfront with full estuary views, seafood and a big patio right at the marina. The weekend brunch view is the whole point.

Sailing Goat — 1900 Stenmark Dr, Richmond. Tucked away at Point San Pablo Harbor, wood fired seafood and coastal plates with free afternoon live music and a view most people never find. Friday to Sunday, worth the drive out. @sailinggoatrestaurant

Five right on the water: Quinn's Lighthouse, Skates, Lake Chalet, Eve's, and the Sailing Goat. Where do you post up at sunset?

item.title: East Bay Sushi and Omakase
item.description: You do not have to cross a bridge for a serious omakase anymore, the East Bay now has counters where the fish flies in from Japan and the price still under
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Sushi and Omakase

You do not have to cross a bridge for a serious omakase anymore, the East Bay now has counters where the fish flies in from Japan and the price still undercuts the city. Eight East Bay sushi and omakase spots.

Delage — Old Oakland. A tiny omakase counter of eight or so courses, California ingredients on Japanese technique, a set menu that sells out. Book the moment seats drop.

Itani Sushi — North Berkeley. A daily changing omakase from chef Kyle Itani with fish flown from Nagasaki, Thursday through Saturday. The special occasion seat.

Kamado Sushi — 1400 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A Gourmet Ghetto room bringing freshness and variety without the pretension, nigiri and rolls done right. The reliable weeknight.

Kirala — 2100 Ward St, Berkeley. A Berkeley sushi and robata institution since 1989, a quiet traditional counter, no gimmicks, worth the wait. The old guard.

Ijji Sushi — Oakland. A sustainability focused sushi bar with a thoughtful omakase and house made touches, small and personal. The conscientious pick.

Kansai — 3945 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. A Piedmont Avenue neighborhood sushi spot with a deep menu and generous cuts, the dependable dinner. The everyday counter.

Geta — 165 41st St, Oakland. A Temescal Japanese spot with sushi and izakaya plates, easy and consistent. The casual option.

Live Sushi Bistro — San Leandro. A south county sushi bar with fresh fish and creative rolls, proof the good sushi is not all in Oakland. The southern outpost.

Eight for the omakase: Delage, Itani, Kamado, Kirala, Ijji, Kansai, Geta, and Live Sushi. Where do you sit at the counter?

item.title: East Bay Oaxacan and Regional Mexican
item.description: Oakland's Mexican food goes far past the taco truck, into Oaxacan moles, Guerrero corn masa, and agave bars pouring mezcal you cannot find anywhere else. E
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Oaxacan and Regional Mexican

Oakland's Mexican food goes far past the taco truck, into Oaxacan moles, Guerrero corn masa, and agave bars pouring mezcal you cannot find anywhere else. Eight East Bay regional Mexican tables.

La Guerrera's Kitchen — 907 Washington St, Oakland. A women led kitchen in Swan's Market grinding heirloom corn for Guerrero style masa, the huaraches and tamales the reason to come. Get the masa.

Agave Uptown — 2135 Franklin St, Oakland. An Oaxacan restaurant for black mole and tlayudas with a deep mezcal list. Order the mole negro.

Comal — 2020 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A downtown Berkeley Oaxacan leaning kitchen with a wood fire, a big back patio, and one of the deepest mezcal bars around. The date night mezcal spot.

Doña — Piedmont Ave, Oakland. The successor to Doña Tomás from the same team, now on Piedmont Avenue for cochinita pibil, mole, and strong margaritas. The old guard.

Nido's BackYard — Embarcadero West, Oakland. The successor to Nido, a Jack London patio kitchen for regional Mexican plates and house masa, warm and unfussy. The neighborhood dinner.

Xolo — 1916 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A downtown taqueria doing bright, fresh tacos and aguas frescas fast and cheap. The quick lunch.

Cholita Linda — 4923 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. The Temescal counter famous for Baja fish tacos and a line out the door. Get the fish taco.

Nieves Cinco de Mayo — 3340 E 12th St, Oakland. A Fruitvale paleteria churning traditional nieves and paletas in flavors like mamey and tuna. The sweet finish.

Eight for the mole: La Guerrera's, Agave Uptown, Comal, Doña, Nido's BackYard, Xolo, Cholita Linda, and Nieves Cinco de Mayo. Where do you start?

item.title: East Bay Korean, Oakland's Koreatown
item.description: Oakland has its own Koreatown, a stretch of Telegraph Avenue locals call KoNo lined with tofu houses, barbecue grills, and late night bowls. Eight East Bay
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Korean, Oakland's Koreatown

Oakland has its own Koreatown, a stretch of Telegraph Avenue locals call KoNo lined with tofu houses, barbecue grills, and late night bowls. Eight East Bay Korean spots.

Pyeong Chang Tofu House — Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A Temescal favorite for bubbling soon tofu soups and a spread of banchan. The comfort soup.

Daol Tofu and Korean BBQ — 4301 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Soon tofu and tabletop barbecue under one roof, the all in one Koreatown stop. Grill and slurp.

Mugunghwa — 4315 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A Telegraph Korean kitchen for stews and grilled meats, a neighborhood standby. The steady dinner.

Ohgane — 3915 Broadway, Oakland. A long running Korean BBQ hall famous for its galbi and buffet of banchan. The big group grill.

Jong Ga House — 372 Grand Ave, Oakland. A Grand Avenue spot near the lake for barbecue and hot stone bibimbap. The lakeside Korean.

Gangnam Jajang — Oakland. A specialist in jajangmyeon, black bean noodles, and other Korean Chinese classics. The noodle craving fix.

Bowl'd Korean BBQ — 1479 Solano Ave, Berkeley. A modern stone bowl bibimbap and barbecue spot on the north Berkeley line. The quick bibimbap.

Spoon Korean Bistro — Berkeley. A casual Berkeley room for stews, bibimbap, and banchan near campus. The student favorite.

Eight for the grill: Pyeong Chang, Daol, Mugunghwa, Ohgane, Jong Ga House, Gangnam Jajang, Bowl'd, and Spoon. Where do you sit down?
