item.title: East Bay Bakeries
item.description: The East Bay quietly out bakes San Francisco, home to the bagels a New York Times critic said rival the best in New York and a worker owned bakery with a c
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Bakeries

The East Bay quietly out bakes San Francisco, home to the bagels a New York Times critic said rival the best in New York and a worker owned bakery with a cult following. Eight East Bay bakeries.

Boichik Bagels — 3170 College Ave, Berkeley. The Rockridge bagelry a New York Times critic said rivals the best New York bagels, boiled and blistered daily. Get there before they sell out.

Starter Bakery — 5804 College Ave, Oakland. The kouign amann specialist that went from wholesale to a beloved cafe, buttery caramelized pastry the star. Order the kouign amann.

La Farine — 6323 College Ave, Oakland. A French neighborhood bakery since 1979 for morning buns and baguettes, an Oakland institution. Get a morning bun.

Arizmendi Bakery — 3265 Lakeshore Ave, Oakland. A worker owned co-op famous for its daily changing gourmet pizza and sourdough by Lake Merritt. Come for the pizza of the day.

Sweet Bar Bakery — 2355 Broadway, Oakland. An Uptown bakery cafe for layer cakes, sticky buns, and a full breakfast. The sit down pastry stop. @sweetbarbakery

Fournée Bakery — 2912 Domingo Ave, Berkeley. A tiny bakery by the Claremont turning out some of the East Bay's best croissants and kouign amann. Worth the line.

Firebrand Artisan Breads — Alameda. The wood fired bread and pastry bakery, now baking in Alameda, croissants and challah among the best around. Grab a loaf. @firebrandbread

Sweet Adeline Bakeshop — 3350 Adeline St, Berkeley. A charming South Berkeley bakeshop for cupcakes, pies, and ice cream sandwiches. The neighborhood sweet.

Eight for the pastry: Boichik, Starter, La Farine, Arizmendi, Sweet Bar, Fournée, Firebrand, and Sweet Adeline. Where do you start?

item.title: East Bay Breweries
item.description: Berkeley's Triple Rock has been brewing since 1986, among the oldest brewpubs in America, and the East Bay around it has grown into a beer scene that rival
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Breweries

Berkeley's Triple Rock has been brewing since 1986, among the oldest brewpubs in America, and the East Bay around it has grown into a beer scene that rivals anywhere. Eight East Bay breweries.

Triple Rock Brewery — 1920 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. One of the oldest brewpubs in America, pouring since 1986 with a rooftop deck. Drink a piece of history.

Fieldwork Brewing — 1160 6th St, Berkeley. The wildly inventive Berkeley taproom that grew to a small empire, a rotating wall of hazy IPAs and fruit sours. Order a flight.

Faction Brewing — 2501 Monarch St, Alameda. A former airfield taproom on Alameda Point with a huge patio and a straight on view of the San Francisco skyline. Drink a hazy with the bay breeze.

Temescal Brewing — 4115 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A neighborhood favorite for hoppy ales and pilsners with a big patio and food trucks. The easy Telegraph hang. @temescalbrewing

Ghost Town Brewing — 1960 Adeline St, Oakland. A West Oakland brewery stacking medals for its IPAs, a raw industrial taproom. The IPA pilgrimage. @ghosttownbrewing

Original Pattern Brewing — 292 4th St, Oakland. An employee owned Jack London district brewery named a top new brewery in the country. The Jack London stop.

Drake's Dealership — 2325 Broadway, Oakland. A sprawling beer garden in an old car dealership with pizza and Drake's beers. The group patio.

Tenma Beer Project — 6510 San Pablo Ave, Oakland. The brewery that took over the old Novel space, a friendly North Oakland taproom pouring house beers. The neighborhood pint.

Eight for the pint: Triple Rock, Fieldwork, Faction, Temescal, Ghost Town, Original Pattern, Drake's Dealership, and Tenma. Where do you start?

item.title: East Bay Coffee Roasters
item.description: American specialty coffee was born at a tiny shop on Berkeley's Vine Street in 1966, where the founders of Starbucks learned to roast from Alfred Peet hims
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Coffee Roasters

American specialty coffee was born at a tiny shop on Berkeley's Vine Street in 1966, where the founders of Starbucks learned to roast from Alfred Peet himself. Eight East Bay coffee roasters.

Peet's Coffee, the original — 2124 Vine St, Berkeley. The 1966 shop where American specialty coffee began, still pouring dark roasts at the corner. Drink from the source.

Red Bay Coffee — 3206 Grand Ave, Oakland. A Black owned Oakland roaster founded in 2014, bright single origins and a mission to match. Try a pour over.

Highwire Coffee Roasters — 5615 College Ave, Oakland. A Rockridge Market Hall roaster from Peet's alums, thoughtful blends and single origins. The Rockridge stop.

Timeless Coffee — 4252 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. A fully vegan roaster and bakery on Piedmont Avenue, house roasts and pastries. Coffee and a vegan treat.

Awaken Cafe and Roasting — 1429 Broadway, Oakland. A downtown community cafe and roaster since 2008 with live music and a big room. The downtown hang.

Bicycle Coffee — 377 2nd St, Oakland. A Jack London roaster that delivers its beans by bike, a small warm cafe. The Jack London cup.

Modern Coffee — 381 19th St, Oakland. A bright Uptown cafe with quality espresso and a calm room to work, weekday mornings the move. The laptop stop.

Blue Bottle Coffee — W Grand Ave, Oakland. The roaster that helped start third wave coffee, back at its Oakland roots. Where the movement began.

Eight for the roast: Peet's original, Red Bay, Highwire, Timeless, Awaken, Bicycle, Modern, and Blue Bottle. Where do you start?

item.title: East Bay Barbecue
item.description: Everett and Jones has been smoking ribs by Jack London Square since 1973, a family recipe that helped put Oakland barbecue on the map. Eight East Bay barbe
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Barbecue

Everett and Jones has been smoking ribs by Jack London Square since 1973, a family recipe that helped put Oakland barbecue on the map. Eight East Bay barbecue joints.

Roderick's Barbecue — 2708 98th Ave, Oakland. A deep East Oakland pit smoking Texas style brisket, ribs, and hot links with Southern sides. Come early before the brisket sells out.

Everett and Jones — 126 Broadway, Oakland. A Jack London Square institution since 1973, hickory smoked ribs and links with a sauce from mild to blazing. Get the ribs and the hot sauce.

Smokin Woods BBQ — 4307 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A Black owned Temescal smokehouse for Texas beef ribs, brisket, and a legendary mac and cheese. Order the beef rib.

KC's Bar-B-Que — 2670 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. A Berkeley classic slinging Memphis style ribs and links for decades. The old school plate.

Smoke Berkeley — 2647 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. A friendly San Pablo Avenue smokehouse with ribs, brisket, and Southern sides. The neighborhood pit.

T-Rex Barbecue — 1300 10th St, Berkeley. A big West Berkeley barbecue and bar with a full smoker and a lively room. The group dinner.

Bo's Barbecue — 3422 Mt Diablo Blvd, Lafayette. A Memphis style pit in Lafayette smoking meats low and slow with a serious beer list. The Lamorinda stop.

Angeline's Louisiana Kitchen — 2261 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A New Orleans style room with smoked and blackened meats and a Bourbon Street feel. The Creole crossover.

Eight for the smoke: Roderick's, Everett and Jones, Smokin Woods, KC's, Smoke Berkeley, T-Rex, Bo's, and Angeline's. Where do you start?

item.title: East Bay Breakfast and Brunch
item.description: Bette's Oceanview Diner has drawn Fourth Street lines for its baked souffle pancake since 1982, and it anchors an East Bay brunch bench as deep as any in t
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Breakfast and Brunch

Bette's Oceanview Diner has drawn Fourth Street lines for its baked souffle pancake since 1982, and it anchors an East Bay brunch bench as deep as any in the country. Eight East Bay breakfast and brunch spots.

Bette's Oceanview Diner — 1807 4th St, Berkeley. A Fourth Street institution since 1982, famous for the baked souffle pancake and a weekend wait worth it. Order the souffle pancake.

Mama's Royal Cafe — 4012 Broadway, Oakland. A quirky, art filled Oakland classic since 1974, huge omelettes and a vintage vibe. Get an omelette and read the walls.

La Note — 2377 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A Provencal cafe for lavender lattes and a lemon gingerbread pancake on a sunny back patio. The French brunch.

Grand Lake Kitchen — 576 Grand Ave, Oakland. A bustling all day cafe and bistro near Lake Merritt for creative scrambles, biscuits, and a full bar brunch. The neighborhood weekend spot.

Lois the Pie Queen — 851 60th St, Oakland. A soul food breakfast institution for decades, grits, catfish, and a slice of sweet potato pie. Add a slice of pie.

Sunny Side Cafe — 1499 Solano Ave, Berkeley. A bright Solano Avenue spot for scrambles and pancakes, a mellow morning table. The easy brunch.

Sequoia Diner — 3719 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. A modern diner in Laurel doing a great biscuit and thoughtful plates. The updated diner.

Jodie's Restaurant — 902 Masonic Ave, Albany. A tiny, beloved Albany breakfast joint where the line forms early for hash and eggs. Get there before the wait.

Eight for brunch: Bette's, Mama's Royal, La Note, Grand Lake Kitchen, Lois the Pie Queen, Sunny Side, Sequoia Diner, and Jodie's. Where do you start?

item.description: Fruitvale's Tacos Sinaloa helped turn International Boulevard into the East Bay's taco corridor, a strip of trucks and taquerias running for miles. Eight E
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Taquerias and Taco Trucks

Fruitvale's Tacos Sinaloa helped turn International Boulevard into the East Bay's taco corridor, a strip of trucks and taquerias running for miles. Eight East Bay taquerias and taco trucks.

Tacos Sinaloa — 2138 International Blvd, Oakland. A Fruitvale pioneer since 1999 with taco trucks in the lot, al pastor and asada off the grill. Order at the truck.

Tacos Oscar — 420 40th St, Oakland. A Temescal taqueria earning a Michelin nod for inventive tacos on house made tortillas. Get the mushroom taco. @tacososcar

Taqueria El Paisa — 4610 International Blvd, Oakland. A Fruitvale favorite for cabeza, lengua, and a loaded salsa bar. Load up at the salsa bar.

Guadalajara Restaurant — 1001 Fruitvale Ave, Oakland. A Fruitvale sit down spot and tequila bar open late for tacos and mariscos. The late night plate.

Mariscos La Costa — Fruitvale, Oakland. A cash only walk up near Fruitvale BART with palm trees and Baja style seafood tacos. Get the fish taco.

Cactus Taqueria — 5642 College Ave, Oakland. A Rockridge favorite for fresh tacos and a big salsa bar, family friendly and fast. The easy weeknight.

Otaez — Oakland. A longtime East Bay taqueria for burritos and tacos, generous and dependable. The reliable order.

Taqueria Los Altos — San Leandro. A south county favorite proving the taco corridor runs past Oakland. The southern stop.

Eight for the taco: Tacos Sinaloa, Tacos Oscar, El Paisa, Guadalajara, Mariscos La Costa, Cactus, Otaez, and Los Altos. Where do you start?

item.content:encoded:
East Bay Breweries and Beer Gardens

The East Bay turned old warehouses and an airfield into some of the Bay Area's best beer, from a West Oakland hop house to an Alameda taproom out on the tarmac. Eight East Bay breweries.

Fieldwork Brewing — 1160 6th St, Berkeley. A West Berkeley taproom rotating a hundred beers a year. Order a hazy IPA flight.

Ghost Town Brewing — 1960 Adeline St, Oakland. A West Oakland taproom of bold hoppy beers. Try the double IPA.

Temescal Brewing — 4115 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A bright Telegraph taproom with a dog friendly patio. Grab the patio.

Original Pattern Brewing — 292 4th St, Oakland. A Jack London district brewery with a big warehouse taproom. Get a crisp lager.

Oakland United Beerworks — 262 2nd St, Oakland. A community minded taproom near Jack London Square. Post up at the bar.

Tenma Beer Project — 6510 San Pablo Ave, Oakland. A cozy North Oakland taproom in the old Novel space with a quiet patio. Try a house lager.

Faction Brewing — 2501 Monarch St, Alameda. An old airfield taproom with a huge patio and skyline view. Sit out on the tarmac.

Drake's Dealership — 2325 Broadway, Oakland. A beer garden in an old car dealership with wood fired pizza. Grab a garden table.

Eight East Bay breweries: Fieldwork, Ghost Town, Temescal, Original Pattern, Oakland United, Tenma, Faction, and Drake's Dealership. Where do you start?

item.content:encoded:

The East Bay quietly became a coffee capital, home to the garage where Blue Bottle started and a Black owned Fruitvale roaster now shipping beans across the country. Eight East Bay coffee roasters.

Timeless Coffee — 4252 Piedmont Ave, Oakland. An all vegan roaster, bakery, and chocolatier. Get an oat latte and a pastry.

Highwire Coffee Roasters — College Ave, Oakland. An East Bay roaster with cafes across Oakland and Berkeley. Grab a Rockridge seat.

Bicycle Coffee Co — 366 13th St, Oakland. A downtown roaster that still delivers beans by bike. Grab a cortado.

Modern Coffee — 381 19th St, Oakland. A sunny Uptown cafe pulling local roasts, weekday mornings. Sit by the window.

Artis Coffee — 1717 4th St, Berkeley. A Fourth Street roaster with precise pour overs. Order a single origin.

1951 Coffee Company — 2410 Channing Way, Berkeley. A nonprofit cafe that trains and employs refugees. Grab a latte for a cause.

item.description: The East Bay eats breakfast at a 1927 Alameda waffle shop and an Oakland cafe that has flipped pancakes for over 50 years, no reservation and no rush. Eigh
item.content:encoded:
East Bay Diners and Breakfast Joints

The East Bay eats breakfast at a 1927 Alameda waffle shop and an Oakland cafe that has flipped pancakes for over 50 years, no reservation and no rush. Eight East Bay diners and breakfast joints.

Ole's Waffle Shop — 1507 Park St, Alameda. A 1927 diner with a horseshoe counter and famous waffles. Get a waffle and bacon.

Mama's Royal Cafe — 4012 Broadway, Oakland. A quirky Oakland breakfast institution of decades, all vintage decor. Order the omelet of the day.

Oceanview Diner — 1807 Fourth St, Berkeley. The Fourth Street pancake house locals have loved for over 40 years. Get the buttermilk pancakes.

La Note — 2377 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A rustic Provencal cafe for a leisurely French breakfast. Order the oatmeal griddle cakes.

Lois the Pie Queen — 851 60th St, Oakland. A soul food breakfast spot serving since 1851 recipes, grits and pie. Get the pie for dessert.

Jodie's Restaurant — 902 Masonic Ave, Albany. A tiny counter with a big personality and huge plates. Squeeze in for the hash.

Hidden City Cafe — 109 Park Pl, Richmond. A Point Richmond corner cafe for a quiet breakfast. Take a window seat.

Jim's Country Style — 5400 Sunol Blvd, Pleasanton. A Tri-Valley diner with omelets named for the regulars. Order a big scramble.

Eight for breakfast: Ole's Waffle Shop, Mama's Royal Cafe, Oceanview Diner, La Note, Lois the Pie Queen, Jodie's, Hidden City Cafe, and Jim's Country Style. Where do you start?

item.content:encoded:
East Bay Wine Bars

The East Bay is in the middle of a natural wine renaissance, from a Grand Avenue shop pouring low intervention bottles to a Temescal spot with a Michelin nod. Eight East Bay wine bars.

Ordinaire — 3354 Grand Ave, Oakland. A natural wine shop and bar that helped start the scene. Ask for a taste before you buy.

The Punchdown — 1737 Broadway, Oakland. An Uptown natural wine bar and bottle shop with a weekly menu. Pour a mystery glass.

Snail Bar — 4935 Shattuck Ave, Oakland. A buzzy Temescal wine bar with a Michelin nod for its little plates. Order the whole spread.

Viridian — 2216 Broadway, Oakland. A stylish Asian inspired bar with wine and cocktails. Sit at the bar.

Bar Shiru — 1611 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A hi fidelity listening bar pairing vinyl with wine. Come for the record sets.

Umami Mart — 815 Broadway, Oakland. A Japanese bottle shop and bar for sake and beer. Try a sake flight.

Vintage Berkeley — 2113 Vine St, Berkeley. A neighborhood wine shop in an old pump house with tastings. Grab a small production bottle.

Prima — 1522 N Main St, Walnut Creek. A longtime Italian restaurant and wine shop with a deep cellar. Browse the wall of bottles.

Eight for wine: Ordinaire, the Punchdown, Snail Bar, Viridian, Bar Shiru, Umami Mart, Vintage Berkeley, and Prima. Where do you start?

East Bay Pizza the Internet Demanded

Every time we post East Bay pizza the comments revolt, so this entire list is the spots you told us we missed. Eight East Bay pizzas.

Gioia Pizzeria — 1586 Hopkins St, Berkeley. A thin crust slice shop off the Hopkins strip that regulars swear beats the famous names. Get a slice of the margherita. A @thejennpfeifferteam add.

Pizzeria da Laura — 2049 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A downtown New York style shop two commenters called the best in the East Bay. Fold a plain cheese slice. A @existential_chef add.

La Val's — 1834 Euclid Ave, Berkeley. A Northside pizza parlor with a theater downstairs, barely changed since the 70s. Order a pitcher and a pepperoni. A @philippgutbrod add.

Benchmark Pizzeria — 1568 Oak View Ave, Kensington. A wood fired neighborhood spot working a natural starter. Get the pie of the day. A @risanye add.

Zachary's Chicago Pizza — 5801 College Ave, Oakland. The deep dish institution, stuffed spinach and mushroom is the move. Order the stuffed deep dish. A @keenethery add.

Melo's Pizza and Pasta — 1660 Contra Costa Blvd, Pleasant Hill. A Contra Costa family shop readers rank with the best. Get a classic combo. A @timcwilkins add.

Devino's Pizza and Pasta — 2221 Morello Ave, Pleasant Hill. The other Pleasant Hill pie named in the same breath as Melo's. Split a large. A @timcwilkins add.

Oceanview To Go — 1807B Fourth St, Berkeley. A Fourth Street counter with a different special pizza every single day. Ask what today's pie is. A @rimaroux add.

item.content:encoded:
East Bay Boba and Milk Tea

The East Bay drinks its boba by the block, from a Rockridge shop that helped start the craze to Fremont strip malls stacked with tea studios. Eight East Bay boba shops.

Boba Guys — 5925 College Ave, Oakland. The Rockridge outpost of the shop that upgraded Bay Area boba. Get the Hong Kong milk tea.

Feng Cha Teahouse — 6180 Jarvis Ave, Newark. A cheese foam and brown sugar boba favorite. Try the cheese foam oolong.

Sunright Tea Studio — 34563 Alvarado Niles Rd, Union City. A tiger sugar style boba with a big following. Order the tiger milk tea.

Yi Fang Taiwan Fruit Tea — 34133 Fremont Blvd, Fremont. A Taiwanese chain known for fresh fruit teas. Get the winter melon fruit tea.

Happy Lemon — 46873 Warm Springs Blvd, Fremont. Home of the salted rock salt cheese topped drinks. Try a rock salt cheese tea.

Wushiland Boba — 46551 Mission Blvd, Fremont. A Taiwanese boba brand with a cult following. Get the wintermelon milk tea.

Ume Tea — 6018 Stevenson Blvd, Fremont. A modern shop for fruit teas and milk foam. Order a strawberry matcha.

Tpumps — 42130 Blacow Rd, Fremont. A build your own sweetness boba spot with a line out the door. Customize your sugar level.

East Bay Bagels

The East Bay is in a bagel boom, led by a Berkeley shop that made bagels worth waiting an hour for. Eight East Bay bagel shops.

Boichik Bagels — 3170 College Ave, Berkeley. The shop that reverse engineered the perfect New York bagel. Get an everything with scallion cream cheese.

Beauty's Bagel Shop — 3838 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. Montreal style wood fired bagels in Temescal. Order a sesame with lox.

Poppy Bagels — 5004 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A sourdough bagel shop with a weekend line. Get the bagel sandwich of the day.

Grand Bakery — 3033 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland. A kosher bakery baking bagels since 1959. Grab a dozen mixed.

Bageltopia — 1401 University Ave, Berkeley. A Berkeley shop rolling classic boiled bagels. Try a jalapeno cheddar.

Berkeley Bagels — 1281 Gilman St, Berkeley. A West Berkeley spot for a chewy morning bagel. Get one toasted with butter.

Alameda Bagels and Donuts — 1227 Park St, Alameda. A Park Street counter for bagels and donuts both. Get one of each.

Bagel Street Cafe — 501 14th St, Oakland. A downtown Oakland cafe for a quick bagel sandwich. Grab a breakfast sandwich to go.

item.title: Mission Burritos and Taquerias
item.description: The most famous burrito in San Francisco has no rice, gets seared on the flat top until the tortilla goes golden, and won its owner a James Beard award. Fi
item.content:encoded:
Mission Burritos and Taquerias

The most famous burrito in San Francisco has no rice, gets seared on the flat top until the tortilla goes golden, and won its owner a James Beard award. Five Mission taquerias worth the pilgrimage.

La Taqueria — 2889 Mission St. The James Beard winning institution, a rice free carnitas burrito crisped dorado style until the tortilla shatters. Closed Monday and Tuesday, so plan around it.

El Farolito — 2779 Mission St. The late night king since 1983, the biggest and cheapest super burrito in the Mission, al pastor off the spit until nearly 3am. The after hours move.

Taqueria Cancun — 2288 Mission St. The vibey corner spot for a classic al pastor burrito with a scoop of guacamole, cheap and open late. The neighborhood workhorse.

La Palma Mexicatessen — 2884 24th St. The masa mothership, handmade tortillas pressed in the window, chicharrones and huaraches and everything from scratch. Buy a stack of tortillas to take home.

Pancho Villa Taqueria — 3071 16th St. A cavernous Mission mainstay with a huge grill and a loaded salsa bar, fast lines and a fat carne asada burrito. The reliable group feed.

Five for the pilgrimage: La Taqueria, El Farolito, Taqueria Cancun, La Palma, and Pancho Villa. Which is the best burrito in the city?

item.title: Dim Sum in San Francisco
item.description: Tucked down a Chinatown alley, Hang Ah Tea Room has served dim sum since 1920. That makes it the oldest dim sum house in America. Five San Francisco spots
item.content:encoded:
Dim Sum in San Francisco

Tucked down a Chinatown alley, Hang Ah Tea Room has served dim sum since 1920. That makes it the oldest dim sum house in America. Five San Francisco spots to push the cart.

Hang Ah Tea Room — 1 Pagoda Pl. Hidden down a Chinatown alley since 1920, the oldest continuously running dim sum house in the country, pork buns and pot stickers in a tiny room. History on a plate.

Yank Sing — 101 Spear St. The polished SoMa classic where the carts roll and the Shanghai soup dumplings and Peking duck are the move. Pricier, and worth it for a treat.

Good Mong Kok Bakery — 1039 Stockton St. The Chinatown takeout window with a line out the door, shrimp har gow and BBQ pork buns for a few dollars, cash only. Grab a bag and eat in Portsmouth Square.

City View Restaurant — 33 Walter U Lum Pl. Old school cart service in a bright Chinatown room, the harder to find dishes wheeled right to your table. Go at opening before the good stuff runs out.

Dragon Beaux — 5700 Geary Blvd. The modern Richmond spot for Hong Kong style dim sum and hot pot, technicolor soup dumplings and roast meats. The dressed up version of the tradition.

Five to push the cart: Hang Ah, Yank Sing, Good Mong Kok, City View, and Dragon Beaux. Har gow or siu mai first?

item.title: San Francisco North Beach Italian
item.description: Molinari has cured salami and stacked sandwiches on Columbus Avenue since 1896, back when North Beach was the landing spot for every Italian in the city. F
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco North Beach Italian

Molinari has cured salami and stacked sandwiches on Columbus Avenue since 1896, back when North Beach was the landing spot for every Italian in the city. Five North Beach classics that never changed.

Molinari Delicatessen — 373 Columbus Ave. The Italian deli since 1896, dry salami hanging from the ceiling and a Renzo Special sandwich big enough for two. Take a number and a hunk of parmigiano.

Tony's Pizza Napoletana — 1570 Stockton St. Tony Gemignani's world championship pizzeria on Washington Square, seven ovens firing every style, the margherita capped at 73 a day. Get there early for one.

Original Joe's — 601 Union St. The maroon booth institution frozen in the fifties, tuxedoed waiters, spicy rigatoni, and a proper martini. Old San Francisco you can still order off a menu.

Sotto Mare — 552 Green St. The tiny loud seafood joint with the best cioppino in North Beach, the Lazy Man's crab and a wait worth taking. Family style and no pretense.

Golden Boy Pizza — 542 Green St. The cash only slice window since 1978, square Sicilian focaccia pizza and cold beer, the after bar tradition. The clam and garlic is the one to get.

Five that never changed: Molinari, Tony's, Original Joe's, Sotto Mare, and Golden Boy. Where do you start a North Beach night?

item.title: San Francisco Seafood and Dungeness Crab
item.description: Swan Oyster Depot has served crab and oysters over the same marble counter since 1912, no reservations, no tables, just a line down Polk Street. Five San F
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco Seafood and Dungeness Crab

Swan Oyster Depot has served crab and oysters over the same marble counter since 1912, no reservations, no tables, just a line down Polk Street. Five San Francisco seafood classics.

Swan Oyster Depot — 1517 Polk St. An eighteen stool marble counter run by the same family since 1912, cracked crab, oysters, and clam chowder, cash and patience required. Get in line by eleven.

Thanh Long — 4101 Judah St. The Sunset original that invented the roasted Dungeness crab and garlic noodles the whole city now copies, bibs on, butter everywhere. Worth the drive to the ocean end.

Anchor Oyster Bar — 579 Castro St. A tiny Castro seafood bar since 1977, the cioppino and the crab louie done right on marble tables. No reservations, small, and beloved.

Scoma's — 1965 Al Scoma Way. The Fisherman's Wharf institution since 1965, boats unloading out back, the Lazy Man's cioppino and whole cracked crab. The classic wharf splurge.

Woodhouse Fish Co — 2073 Market St. A casual New England style fish house, lobster rolls, crab boils, and a raw bar, the everyday seafood fix without the wharf prices.

Five for the crab: Swan Oyster Depot, Thanh Long, Anchor Oyster Bar, Scoma's, and Woodhouse. Cracked crab or cioppino?

item.title: San Francisco Ice Cream
item.description: The very first Swensen's opened on a Russian Hill corner in 1948, and it still hand cranks its ice cream in the front window. Five San Francisco scoop shop
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco Ice Cream

The very first Swensen's opened on a Russian Hill corner in 1948, and it still hand cranks its ice cream in the front window. Five San Francisco scoop shops worth the cone.

Swensen's — 1999 Hyde St. The 1948 original at the top of the cable car line, hand cranked in the window, sundaes and the Sticky Chewy Chocolate under a striped awning. Where the whole chain began.

Bi-Rite Creamery — 3692 18th St. The Mission line out the door for salted caramel and honey lavender, organic and made in tiny batches next to the market. Worth the wait, always. @biritesf

Mitchell's Ice Cream — 688 San Jose Ave. Family run since the fifties, forty flavors a day including the mango and avocado that put it on the map. Take a number and a pint.

Salt and Straw — 586 Hayes St. The Hayes Valley shop for wildly inventive seasonal flavors, olive oil and honey balsamic, samples until you decide. Bring your curiosity.

Garden Creamery — 3566 20th St. A Mission scoop shop of Asian inspired flavors, ube and black sesame and Vietnamese coffee, rich and not too sweet. The mochi is the move.

Five for the cone: Swensen's, Bi-Rite, Mitchell's, Salt and Straw, and Garden Creamery. Which scoop wins?

item.title: San Francisco Cocktail Bars and Speakeasies
item.description: Behind a plain door in Hayes Valley hides a multi level tiki den holding the largest rum selection in the United States, north of 400 bottles. Five San Fra
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco Cocktail Bars and Speakeasies

Behind a plain door in Hayes Valley hides a multi level tiki den holding the largest rum selection in the United States, north of 400 bottles. Five San Francisco bars for a serious cocktail.

Smuggler's Cove — 650 Gough St. A multi story tiki shipwreck with hundreds of rums and a menu of tropical drinks, flaming and garnished to the hilt. Order the Dead Reckoning and settle in.

Bourbon and Branch — 501 Jones St. A working speakeasy in a real 1920s Prohibition space, reservations and a password at an unmarked door, house rules on the wall. Ask for the library.

Pacific Cocktail Haven — 550 Sutter St. The downtown temple of precise, playful cocktails, the wasabi Trust Fall a signature, always on the world's best lists. Sit at the bar and let them cook.

Trick Dog — 3010 20th St. A Mission cocktail bar with a cult menu that reinvents itself around a wild new theme twice a year, plus a great burger. Come for the drinks, stay for the design.

Comstock Saloon — 155 Columbus Ave. A restored Barbary Coast saloon on the edge of North Beach, classic cocktails, a free lunch tradition, and a player piano. Old San Francisco in a glass.

Five for the cocktail: Smuggler's Cove, Bourbon and Branch, Pacific Cocktail Haven, Trick Dog, and Comstock Saloon. What are you ordering?

item.title: San Francisco South Bay Vietnamese, Pho and Banh Mi (San Jose)
item.description: San Jose has among the largest Vietnamese communities outside Vietnam, and the banh mi on Story Road runs a few dollars and rivals anything in Saigon. Five
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco South Bay Vietnamese, Pho and Banh Mi (San Jose)

San Jose has among the largest Vietnamese communities outside Vietnam, and the banh mi on Story Road runs a few dollars and rivals anything in Saigon. Five South Bay stops for pho and banh mi.

Pho Ha Noi — 969 Story Rd. The Little Saigon pho house with the line out the door, a clean northern style broth and rare beef, in the rebuilt Vietnam Town plaza. Follow the crowd.

Huong Lan Sandwiches — 1655 Tully Rd. A banh mi and deli powerhouse, the cold cut combo and grilled pork on a crackly baguette for a few bucks, plus a case of Vietnamese sides. Stock the fridge.

Duc Huong Sandwiches — 1020 Story Rd. A Story Road banh mi legend, house made cha and pate on airy bread, cheap, fast, and always right. Get the special. @duchuongsandwiches

Cali Sandwiches — 972 Story Rd. A local favorite for grilled pork and lemongrass chicken banh mi with pickled everything, a quick Little Saigon stop. Two will feed you for a fiver.

Lee's Sandwiches — 2307 McKee Rd. The San Jose born chain that made banh mi mainstream, the croissant combo and a Vietnamese iced coffee to go. The reliable road trip fuel.

Five for pho and banh mi: Pho Ha Noi, Huong Lan, Duc Huong, Cali, and Lee's. Where is your Story Road order?

item.title: San Francisco Tomales Bay Oysters (North Bay)
item.description: On the shore of Tomales Bay you can shuck oysters pulled from the water an hour earlier, at picnic tables right on the farm that grew them. Five North Bay
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco Tomales Bay Oysters (North Bay)

On the shore of Tomales Bay you can shuck oysters pulled from the water an hour earlier, at picnic tables right on the farm that grew them. Five North Bay stops for the freshest oysters in California.

Hog Island Oyster Co — 20215 Shoreline Hwy, Marshall. The farm itself, shuck your own at bayside tables or sit at the Boat Oyster Bar, oysters pulled from the water out front. Reserve for weekends. @hogislandoysterco

Tomales Bay Oyster Company — 15479 Shoreline Hwy, Marshall. The oldest shellfish farm in the state, since 1909, buy them unshucked by the dozen and grill them on the provided pits. Bring your own everything.

The Marshall Store — 19225 Shoreline Hwy, Marshall. A tiny oyster bar and smokehouse over the water, barbecued oysters with chipotle butter and a stool with a view. Order at the counter.

Tony's Seafood — 18863 Shoreline Hwy, Marshall. The 1948 roadhouse reborn by the Hog Island family, wood grilled oysters and fish on a deck over Tomales Bay. The sit down version.

Nick's Cove — 23240 Shoreline Hwy, Marshall. A restored roadhouse and oyster bar with waterfront cabins, barbecued oysters and a dock to walk out on. Make a night of it.

Five for the shuck: Hog Island, Tomales Bay Oyster Co, the Marshall Store, Tony's Seafood, and Nick's Cove. Raw or barbecued?

item.title: San Francisco Wine Country Towns (North Bay)
item.description: You do not need a car to taste wine in Healdsburg, the plaza is ringed by tasting rooms and Michelin kitchens all within a couple of walkable blocks. Five
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco Wine Country Towns (North Bay)

You do not need a car to taste wine in Healdsburg, the plaza is ringed by tasting rooms and Michelin kitchens all within a couple of walkable blocks. Five wine country towns worth the drive north.

Healdsburg — Sonoma County. A walkable plaza ringed by tasting rooms, Michelin restaurants, and the Russian River a few minutes away. The polished heart of Sonoma wine country. Park once and stroll.

Sonoma — Sonoma Valley. The historic plaza where California wine was born, the old mission, tasting rooms, and a cheese shop on the square. History and wine in one town. Start at the plaza.

Yountville — Napa Valley. A tiny town with more Michelin stars per block than almost anywhere, the French Laundry, Bouchon Bakery, and a walkable main street. Book dinner months ahead.

Glen Ellen — Sonoma Valley. A rustic creekside hamlet in Jack London country, small tasting rooms and the author's ranch in the hills above. The quiet, woodsy alternative. Slow down here.

Calistoga — Napa Valley. The top of the valley known for hot springs, mud baths, and an old west main street, wineries without the down valley crowds. Soak after the tasting.

Five wine country towns: Healdsburg, Sonoma, Yountville, Glen Ellen, and Calistoga. Which town for the weekend?

item.title: San Francisco Bakeries and Sourdough
item.description: Boudin has kept the same sourdough mother starter alive since the Gold Rush in 1849. That makes it the oldest continuously operating business in San Franci
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco Bakeries and Sourdough

Boudin has kept the same sourdough mother starter alive since the Gold Rush in 1849. That makes it the oldest continuously operating business in San Francisco. Five bakeries for the city's daily bread.

Boudin Bakery — 160 Jefferson St. The 1849 original at Fisherman's Wharf, sourdough from a mother starter older than the state, baked into bread bowls and crab shapes in the window. The origin loaf. @boudinbakery

Tartine Bakery — 600 Guerrero St. The Mission line that never quits since 2002, morning buns and country loaves that rewrote Bay Area baking. Come at open or wait an hour. @tartinebakery

Arsicault Bakery — 397 Arguello Blvd. A tiny Inner Richmond shop whose croissant was named the best in America, buttery and shattering. Get there early, they sell out. @arsicaultbakery

b — patisserie. 2821 California St. The Pacific Heights temple of the kouign amann, caramelized and flaky, plus pristine French pastry. The pastry case is a work of art.

Jane the Bakery — 1881 Geary Blvd. A Lower Fillmore bakery turning out dozens of house breads and laminated pastries daily, plus a proper sandwich. The all day neighborhood stop. @janethebakery

Five for the daily bread: Boudin, Tartine, Arsicault, b. patisserie, and Jane. Which loaf do you line up for?

item.title: San Francisco Coffee Roasters
item.description: When Ritual opened on Valencia Street in 2005 with a giant red logo and single origin beans, it lit the fuse on San Francisco's whole third wave coffee sce
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco Coffee Roasters

When Ritual opened on Valencia Street in 2005 with a giant red logo and single origin beans, it lit the fuse on San Francisco's whole third wave coffee scene. Five San Francisco roasters worth the pilgrimage.

Ritual Coffee Roasters — 1026 Valencia St. The Mission roaster that sparked the city's specialty scene, bright single origins and a buzzing corner cafe. Where the third wave started. @ritualcoffee

Sightglass Coffee — 270 Seventh St. A soaring SoMa roastery in an old warehouse, the beans roasting behind the counter and a mezzanine to watch from. The flagship experience. @sightglass

Four Barrel Coffee — 375 Valencia St. A Mission roaster with no wifi on purpose, a wood and leather room built for actually talking to people. Old school by design.

Andytown Coffee Roasters — 3655 Lawton St. The Outer Sunset roaster famous for the Snowy Plover, espresso and sparkling water over cream, Irish soda bread on the side. Worth the trek to the beach. @andytownsf

Saint Frank Coffee — 2340 Polk St. A bright Russian Hill flagship of clean, precise coffee in a minimalist space, the cortado dialed in. The polished cup.

Five for the pilgrimage: Ritual, Sightglass, Four Barrel, Andytown, and Saint Frank. Where is your pour over?

item.title: San Francisco Peninsula Dim Sum
item.description: Koi Palace in Daly City seats 400 around a koi pond and live seafood tanks, and dim sum fans drive in from across the region for a weekend cart. Five Penin
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco Peninsula Dim Sum

Koi Palace in Daly City seats 400 around a koi pond and live seafood tanks, and dim sum fans drive in from across the region for a weekend cart. Five Peninsula dim sum halls worth the wait.

Koi Palace — 365 Gellert Blvd, Daly City. The Bay Area dim sum crown, a koi pond and seafood tanks and carts of har gow and soup dumplings, a wait that is part of the ritual. Put your name in and hover.

Hong Kong Palace — 300 El Camino Real, Millbrae. A Millbrae banquet hall doing classic carts and made to order plates, the roast meats and shrimp dumplings the move. Reliable and roomy.

New SF Asian Pearl Peninsula — 1671 El Camino Real, Millbrae. A big bright Millbrae room of Cantonese dim sum and seafood, the egg tarts and char siu bao fresh from the kitchen. Go with a group.

Dim Sum King — 99 Skyline Plaza, Daly City. A no frills Daly City takeout counter for cheap, fast dim sum by the box, the sticky rice and the buns for a few dollars. Grab and go.

The Kitchen — 279 El Camino Real, Millbrae. A cavernous Millbrae banquet hall with full cart service on weekends, the whole parade of dumplings and greens wheeled past. Old school dim sum theater.

Five to push the cart: Koi Palace, Hong Kong Palace, New Asian Pearl, Dim Sum King, and The Kitchen. Har gow first?

item.title: San Francisco South Bay South Indian, Dosa and Chaat
item.description: Saravanaa Bhavan in Sunnyvale is part of the world's largest South Indian restaurant chain, and the dosas here rival the ones in Chennai. Five South Bay st
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco South Bay South Indian, Dosa and Chaat

Saravanaa Bhavan in Sunnyvale is part of the world's largest South Indian restaurant chain, and the dosas here rival the ones in Chennai. Five South Bay stops for dosa, idli, and chaat.

Saravanaa Bhavan — 1305 S Mary Ave, Sunnyvale. The Sunnyvale outpost of the global South Indian giant since 1981, paper dosas the length of your arm and filter coffee to finish. The gold standard. @saravanaabhavanbayarea

Chaat Bhavan — 976 E El Camino Real, Sunnyvale. A pure vegetarian favorite for the chaat, the pani puri and the pav bhaji, plus a full dosa lineup. Loud, cheap, and packed.

Komala Vilas — 1020 E El Camino Real, Sunnyvale. A pocket friendly tiffin spot beloved for the breakfast idlis and coconut chutney, the vada and the uttapam done right. The morning move.

Madras Cafe — 1177 W El Camino Real, Sunnyvale. A longtime Sunnyvale room for upma, uttappam, and crisp dosas, the kind of tiffin place regulars have gone to for years. Unfussy and consistent.

Ulavacharu Tiffins — Milpitas. A quick bite favorite for the ulavacharu masala dosa and podi idly, bold Andhra flavors and fast service. Worth the Milpitas stop.

Five for the dosa: Saravanaa Bhavan, Chaat Bhavan, Komala Vilas, Madras Cafe, and Ulavacharu. Which tiffin is your regular?

item.title: San Francisco Napa Beyond the Wine
item.description: You can spend a whole day in Napa without a single wine tasting, starting at Oxbow Public Market where oyster bars, taco counters, and a famous English muf
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco Napa Beyond the Wine

You can spend a whole day in Napa without a single wine tasting, starting at Oxbow Public Market where oyster bars, taco counters, and a famous English muffin share a roof. Five Napa stops that are not about the wine.

Oxbow Public Market — 610 First St, Napa. The Ferry Building of Napa, a food hall of oysters, tacos, cheese, and coffee under one roof, plus the Model Bakery. Graze your way through.

The Model Bakery — Oxbow Public Market, Napa. The nearly century old bakery inside Oxbow famous for the English muffin Oprah put on her list, griddled and dripping with butter. Get there before they sell out.

Gott's Roadside — 644 First St, Napa. The James Beard winning roadside burger stand born in the valley, ahi tuna burgers and shakes on a big patio. The all American lunch.

CIA at Copia — 500 First St, Napa. The Culinary Institute's food and wine campus with gardens, exhibits, a restaurant, and the giant Chuck Williams kitchen collection, much of it free. Foodie heaven.

Downtown Napa Riverfront — First Street, Napa. A walkable riverside promenade of restaurants, a historic mill, and public art along the Napa River. The easy stroll after lunch.

Five that are not about the wine: Oxbow, the Model Bakery, Gott's, CIA at Copia, and the Riverfront. Where do you start the day?

item.title: San Francisco South Bay Ramen
item.description: Ramen Nagi lets you build your bowl from scratch, choosing broth richness, noodle firmness, garlic, and spice, and the lines at its Santa Clara mall counte
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco South Bay Ramen

Ramen Nagi lets you build your bowl from scratch, choosing broth richness, noodle firmness, garlic, and spice, and the lines at its Santa Clara mall counter prove it works. Eight South Bay ramen shops worth the wait.

Ramen Nagi — Westfield Valley Fair, Santa Clara. The customizable phenom, build your Butao King from broth to noodle firmness, lines that move fast once you order. The choose your own bowl.

Tanto — 1063 E El Camino Real, Sunnyvale. A beloved Sunnyvale izakaya of more than twenty years, ramen bowls, donburi, and a long list of small plates. The reliable bowl.

Orenchi Ramen and Sushi — State Street Market, Los Altos. The beloved Orenchi tonkotsu reborn in the Los Altos food hall, the rich pork bone broth that built a cult following. The classic, new address. @orenchi.ramen_sushi

Halu — 245 E Taylor St, San Jose. A tiny Japantown izakaya papered in beer labels doing ramen and skewers, cash only and always packed. Squeeze in and order the yakitori too.

Santouka — 675 Saratoga Ave, San Jose. The Hokkaido chain's outpost inside the Mitsuwa market, a delicate shio tonkotsu with a salted plum, a food court gem. Shop the market after.

Ramen Izakaya Yu-Gen — San Jose. A ramen and small plates spot slow cooking its tonkotsu broth for sixteen hours, rich and deep, with izakaya bites alongside. Order skewers with the bowl.

Ramen Seas — Sunnyvale. A Sunnyvale favorite for a clean, balanced tonkotsu and a tidy dining room, the reliable South Bay bowl without the mall lines. The easy weeknight.

Tori Ramen — San Jose. A chicken based ramen specialist, a lighter torigara broth for those who skip pork, plus tsukemen to dip. The different bowl.

Eight for the bowl: Ramen Nagi, Tanto, Orenchi, Halu, Santouka, Yu-Gen, Ramen Seas, and Tori Ramen. Tonkotsu or shio?

item.title: San Francisco South Bay Asian Eats, Dumplings and Boba
item.description: Din Tai Fung folds each soup dumpling with eighteen pleats and steams it to order, and the wait at its Valley Fair counter runs past an hour on weekends. E
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco South Bay Asian Eats, Dumplings and Boba

Din Tai Fung folds each soup dumpling with eighteen pleats and steams it to order, and the wait at its Valley Fair counter runs past an hour on weekends. Eight South Bay stops for dumplings, noodles, and boba.

Din Tai Fung — Westfield Valley Fair, Santa Clara. The Taiwanese soup dumpling giant, eighteen pleat xiao long bao and truffle dumplings worth the wait. Put your name down and shop.

Marugame Udon — Westfield Valley Fair, Santa Clara. Fresh udon pulled and cut in front of you with a tempura bar to load up, cheap, fast, and satisfying. Watch the noodles get made.

Baekjeong — Westfield Valley Fair, Santa Clara. The Korean BBQ juggernaut with tableside grills and a wall of banchan, cook your own galbi with a crowd. Come hungry with friends.

Darda Seafood — 296 Barber Ln, Milpitas. A famous halal Chinese kitchen for hand pulled beef noodle soup and lamb, a Milpitas legend tucked in an office park. Order the beef noodle.

85C Bakery Cafe — Cupertino. The Taiwanese bakery and drink chain, sea salt coffee and a case of pillowy buns for pocket change. Grab a tray and tongs.

Meet Fresh — Cupertino. The Taiwanese dessert shop for grass jelly, taro balls, and shaved ice, warm or cold and never too sweet. The after dinner move.

Shanghai Dumpling Shop — Milpitas. A no frills Milpitas favorite for xiao long bao and pan fried buns at half the mall price, cash and a wait. The local secret.

Ranch 99, Milpitas Square — Milpitas. The flagship Asian supermarket anchoring a plaza of food stalls, a live seafood counter and a food court crawl. Shop and graze.

Eight in the South Bay: Din Tai Fung, Marugame, Baekjeong, Darda, 85C, Meet Fresh, Shanghai Dumpling, and Ranch 99. Which dumpling wins?

item.title: Bay Area Food Halls
item.description: The Bay Area turned old markets, army mess halls, and ferry terminals into food halls, letting you graze a dozen local makers under a roof. Eight Bay Area
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Food Halls

The Bay Area turned old markets, army mess halls, and ferry terminals into food halls, letting you graze a dozen local makers under a roof. Eight Bay Area food halls.

Ferry Building Marketplace — San Francisco. The 1898 ferry terminal reborn as the region's grandest food hall with Hog Island, Acme, and a Saturday farmers market. Come Saturday morning.

Oxbow Public Market — 610 1st St, Napa. A downtown Napa hall of oyster bars, taquerias, and cheese counters by the river. Slurp oysters and browse.

Swan's Market — 510 9th St, Oakland. Oakland's central market, over 100 years old, now stalls of tacos, oysters, and Caribbean food in Old Oakland. Graze a few counters.

Public Market Emeryville — 5959 Shellmound St, Emeryville. A big international food hall of dozens of stalls from dumplings to poke. Something for everyone.

San Pedro Square Market — 87 N San Pedro St, San Jose. A lively downtown San Jose hall with a dozen plus food stalls, bars, and live music. The night out.

Rockridge Market Hall — 5655 College Ave, Oakland. A gourmet cluster of a fishmonger, cheese shop, bakery, and wine, upscale grazing. Build a dinner.

The Mess Hall — Presidio, San Francisco. A former army mess hall in the Presidio newly opened as a food hall by the Tunnel Tops. Eat with a park view.

Marin Country Mart — 2257 Larkspur Landing Cir, Larkspur. An open air market by the ferry with food stalls, a farmers market, and live music. Graze by the water.

Eight food halls: the Ferry Building, Oxbow, Swan's Market, Public Market Emeryville, San Pedro Square, Rockridge Market Hall, the Mess Hall, and Marin Country Mart. Where do you start?

item.title: Bay Area Dim Sum
item.description: Koi Palace in Daly City is regularly called the best dim sum in the country, with weekend waits that run past an hour for its live seafood and swan shaped
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Dim Sum

Koi Palace in Daly City is regularly called the best dim sum in the country, with weekend waits that run past an hour for its live seafood and swan shaped taro puffs. Eight Bay Area dim sum halls.

Koi Palace — 365 Gellert Blvd, Daly City. The famous Cantonese banquet hall, live seafood tanks and creative dim sum, weekend waits worth it. Put your name in early.

Yank Sing — 101 Spear St, San Francisco. A polished downtown institution rolling carts of Shanghai dumplings and pork buns. Flag down the xiao long bao.

Hong Kong Lounge II — 3300 Geary Blvd, San Francisco. A packed Richmond banquet room of lazy susans and classic carts. Come with a group and spin.

Dragon Beaux — 5700 Geary Blvd, San Francisco. A modern Hong Kong spot known for the swan and piggy shaped dumplings and har gow. Order the swan puffs.

Good Mong Kok Bakery — 1039 Stockton St, San Francisco. A cash only Chinatown counter with a line for cheap, fresh steamed buns and dumplings to go. Grab a box for the park.

East Ocean Seafood — 1713 Webster St, Alameda. A big island banquet hall with carts on the weekend, a bayside dim sum classic. Go for the carts.

New Asian Pearl — Millbrae. A Peninsula banquet hall for cart dim sum near the airport, a Millbrae standby. The Peninsula stop.

Dynasty Chinese Seafood — San Jose. A South Bay banquet hall rolling carts of shu mai and turnip cake. The South Bay spread.

Eight for dim sum: Koi Palace, Yank Sing, Hong Kong Lounge II, Dragon Beaux, Good Mong Kok, East Ocean, New Asian Pearl, and Dynasty. Where do you start?

item.title: Bay Area Pizza
item.description: The Bay Area's most decorated pizzaiolo has won the world championship in Naples, but the best slice around might be a Berkeley collective with a line down
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Pizza

The Bay Area's most decorated pizzaiolo has won the world championship in Naples, but the best slice around might be a Berkeley collective with a line down the sidewalk and a single pie a day. Eight Bay Area pizzerias.

Tony's Pizza Napoletana — 1570 Stockton St, SF. The North Beach temple from a world champion pizzaiolo, many styles from many ovens. Order the Margherita, limited daily.

Cheese Board Pizza — 1512 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. The Berkeley collective with one vegetarian pie a day, a jazz combo, and a line down the block. Get whatever is on.

Zachary's Chicago Pizza — 5801 College Ave, Oakland. The Rockridge deep dish institution, stuffed crust worth the wait. Get the stuffed spinach and mushroom.

Pizzeria Delfina — 3611 18th St, SF. The Mission Neapolitan spot behind Delfina, blistered thin crust. Get the Napoletana.

Del Popolo — 855 Bush St, SF. A wood fired standout that started as a shipping container oven, now a glass walled room. Order the Margherita.

Flour and Water Pizza Shop — 702 Valencia St, SF. A slice shop from the Flour and Water team, thick square Sicilian and pepperoni. Grab a square.

Little Star Pizza — 400 Valencia St, SF. A San Francisco deep dish favorite with a cornmeal crust. Get the Classic deep dish.

Emilia's Pizzeria — 2995 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A tiny Berkeley shop serving New York style by preorder, revered. Preorder a whole pie.

Eight Bay Area pizzerias: Tony's, the Cheese Board, Zachary's, Pizzeria Delfina, Del Popolo, Flour and Water, Little Star, and Emilia's. Where do you start?

item.description: The Bay Area's ramen obsession runs from a Japantown counter with an hour wait to a Sonoma shop making its own noodles from local grain. Eight Bay Area ram
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Ramen

The Bay Area's ramen obsession runs from a Japantown counter with an hour wait to a Sonoma shop making its own noodles from local grain. Eight Bay Area ramen bowls.

Marufuku Ramen — 1581 Webster St, SF. A Japantown favorite with silky Hakata tonkotsu and a long wait. Get the tonkotsu.

Hinodeya — 1737 Buchanan St, SF. A Japantown shop known for a lighter dashi based broth. Try the dashi ramen.

Iza Ramen — 237 Fillmore St, SF. A Lower Haight bowl shop that grew from a pop up. Order the spicy miso.

Ramen Shop — 5812 College Ave, Oakland. A Rockridge spot from Chez Panisse alums with seasonal bowls. Get whatever is seasonal.

Ramen Nagi — 541 Bryant St, Palo Alto. A build your own Butao bowl with rich broth, always a line. Customize the Butao King.

Ramen Dojo — 805 S B St, San Mateo. A tiny San Mateo counter with a cult following and a wait. Go early or wait.

Orenchi Ramen — 3540 Homestead Rd, Santa Clara. A South Bay original famous for its tonkotsu. Line up before it opens.

Ramen Gaijin — 6948 Sebastopol Ave, Sebastopol. A Sonoma County shop making noodles from local grain. Try the shoyu.

Eight Bay Area ramen bowls: Marufuku, Hinodeya, Iza, Ramen Shop, Ramen Nagi, Ramen Dojo, Orenchi, and Ramen Gaijin. Which bowl first?

item.title: Bay Area Bakeries and Croissants
item.description: The Bay Area might bake the best croissant in America, and the reigning champions run from a corner shop in the foggy Richmond to a wood oven in Petaluma.
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Bakeries and Croissants

The Bay Area might bake the best croissant in America, and the reigning champions run from a corner shop in the foggy Richmond to a wood oven in Petaluma. Eight Bay Area bakeries.

Arsicault Bakery — 397 Arguello Blvd, SF. A Richmond corner shop whose almond croissant won national best new bakery. Get the almond croissant.

Tartine Bakery — 600 Guerrero St, SF. The Mission institution with a morning bun worth the line. Get a morning bun.

Jane the Bakery — 1881 Geary Blvd, SF. A big airy bakery and cafe with house breads and pastries. Grab a loaf and a coffee.

Neighbor Bakehouse — 2343 3rd St, SF. A Dogpatch bakery famous for its everything croissant. Get the everything croissant.

Fournée Bakery — 2912 Domingo Ave, Berkeley. A tiny Berkeley shop by the Claremont with a killer kouign amann. Go early, it sells out.

Starter Bakery — 3418 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. An Oakland bakery known for its kouign amann and canelés. Try the kouign amann.

Model Bakery — 1357 Main St, St Helena. A Napa Valley bakery whose English muffin became famous. Get the English muffin.

Della Fattoria — 141 Petaluma Blvd N, Petaluma. A wood oven bakery and cafe in downtown Petaluma. Grab a slab of focaccia.

Eight Bay Area bakeries: Arsicault, Tartine, Jane, Neighbor Bakehouse, Fournée, Starter, Model Bakery, and Della Fattoria. Where do you start?

item.title: Bay Area Oyster Bars and Seafood
item.description: The Bay Area slurps oysters at a marble counter that has barely changed since 1912 and cracks crab on a Tomales Bay dock, some of the best seafood on the c
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Oyster Bars and Seafood

The Bay Area slurps oysters at a marble counter that has barely changed since 1912 and cracks crab on a Tomales Bay dock, some of the best seafood on the coast. Eight Bay Area oyster and seafood spots.

Swan Oyster Depot — 1517 Polk St, SF. The 1912 marble counter for oysters and cracked crab, cash only. Get the combo.

Hog Island Oyster Co — 1 Ferry Building, SF. The Ferry Building raw bar pulling Tomales Bay oysters with a water view. Do a dozen.

Anchor Oyster Bar — 579 Castro St, SF. A Castro seafood counter since 1977, cioppino and oysters. Get the cioppino.

Sotto Mare — 552 Green St, SF. A North Beach seafood joint famous for its crab cioppino. Order the cioppino.

Woodhouse Fish Co — 2073 Market St, SF. A New England style fish shack for lobster rolls and oysters. Get a lobster roll.

Scoma's — 1965 Al Scoma Way, SF. A Fisherman's Wharf seafood institution since 1965, pier to plate. Order the Dungeness.

Alamar Kitchen — 100 Grand Ave, Oakland. An Oakland seafood boil spot for shrimp and crab by the bag. Get a boil bag.

Nick's Cove — 23240 Highway 1, Marshall. A Tomales Bay oyster roadhouse on the water. Slurp oysters on the dock.

Eight for seafood: Swan Oyster Depot, Hog Island, Anchor Oyster Bar, Sotto Mare, Woodhouse, Scoma's, Alamar, and Nick's Cove. Where do you start?

item.title: Bay Area Ethiopian
item.description: The Bay Area's best Ethiopian food clusters along a single stretch of Oakland's Telegraph Avenue, where you scoop spicy stews with spongy injera and no for
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Ethiopian

The Bay Area's best Ethiopian food clusters along a single stretch of Oakland's Telegraph Avenue, where you scoop spicy stews with spongy injera and no fork in sight. Eight Bay Area Ethiopian tables.

Cafe Colucci — 6427 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A family run room since 1991 with old school stews and a combo platter. Get the veggie combo.

Cafe Romanat — 462 21st St, Oakland. A warm favorite for spicy tibs and honey wine. Order the tibs.

Enssaro — 357 Grand Ave, Oakland. A Grand Avenue spot for a big injera combo. Share a platter.

Asmara — 5020 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A longtime Eritrean and Ethiopian kitchen. Try the zilzil tibs.

Barcote — 6430 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A Temescal favorite for kitfo and combos. Get the kitfo.

New Eritrea Restaurant and Bar — 907 Irving St, SF. An Inner Sunset stalwart for injera and stews. Order the vegetarian combo.

Zeni Ethiopian — 1320 Saratoga Ave, San Jose. A South Bay spot with spicy red lentils and gored gored. Get the gored gored.

Walia Ethiopian — 2208 Business Cir, San Jose. A San Jose favorite for tibs and injera. Share the combo.

Eight for injera: Cafe Colucci, Cafe Romanat, Enssaro, Asmara, Barcote, New Eritrea, Zeni, and Walia. Where do you start?

item.description: The Bay Area's barbecue runs deep, from an Oakland institution smoking ribs by Jack London Square to a Divisadero backyard pit with a cult burger, Texas br
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Barbecue

The Bay Area's barbecue runs deep, from an Oakland institution smoking ribs by Jack London Square to a Divisadero backyard pit with a cult burger, Texas brisket to Memphis ribs across the whole bay. Eight Bay Area barbecue joints.

Roderick's Barbecue — 2708 98th Ave, Oakland. A deep East Oakland pit turning out Texas style brisket and hot links, go before it sells out. Get the brisket early.

Smokin Woods BBQ — 4307 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. An Oakland smokehouse loved for ribs and burnt ends. Order the burnt ends.

Everett and Jones Barbeque — 126 Broadway, Oakland. A Jack London Square institution with a family recipe sauce. Get the links.

Phat Matt's BBQ — 4622 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A neighborhood spot for tri tip and brisket plates. Order the tri tip.

KC's BBQ — 2613 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. A Berkeley classic smoking ribs for decades. Get a rib plate.

4505 Burgers and BBQ — 705 Divisadero St, SF. A Divisadero backyard smoker for brisket and a cult burger. Try the brisket.

Memphis Minnie's — 576 Haight St, SF. A Lower Haight barbecue joint for pulled pork and ribs. Order the pulled pork.

Smoking Pig BBQ — 1144 N 4th St, San Jose. A South Bay smokehouse for brisket and links. Get the combo plate.

Eight for smoke: Roderick's, Smokin Woods, Everett and Jones, Phat Matt's, KC's, 4505, Memphis Minnie's, and Smoking Pig. Where do you start?

item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Vietnamese

The Bay Area chases Vietnamese food from a clear northern pho in the Financial District to San Jose banh mi lines that run out the door, a scene as deep as it gets. Eight Bay Area Vietnamese stops.

Turtle Tower — 220 California St, SF. The FiDi shop for clear northern style pho ga since 1999. Order the pho ga.

Bodega Bistro — 607 Larkin St, SF. A Little Saigon room for Hanoi street food and cha ca. Get the cha ca.

Yummy Yummy — 1015 Irving St, SF. An Inner Sunset favorite for bun and pho, always packed. Get the bun bo Hue.

Tay Ho — 344 12th St, Oakland. An Oakland spot known for banh cuon and com tam. Order the banh cuon.

Binh Minh Quan — 8045 International Blvd, Oakland. An International Boulevard pho house with a big menu. Get a bowl of pho.

Vung Tau — 535 E Santa Clara St, San Jose. A San Jose institution for a wide Vietnamese spread. Try the shaking beef.

Huong Lan — 1655 Tully Rd, San Jose. The banh mi and deli line that stretches out the door. Grab a banh mi.

Rose International Market — 1060 Castro St, Mountain View. A market and banh mi counter with a cult following. Order a banh mi.

Eight for Vietnamese: Turtle Tower, Bodega Bistro, Yummy Yummy, Tay Ho, Binh Minh Quan, Vung Tau, Huong Lan, and Rose Market. Where do you start?

item.title: Bay Area Korean
item.description: The Bay Area's Korean heart beats along Oakland's Telegraph and Broadway, where charcoal grills and bubbling tofu stews have drawn crowds for decades. Eigh
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Korean

The Bay Area's Korean heart beats along Oakland's Telegraph and Broadway, where charcoal grills and bubbling tofu stews have drawn crowds for decades. Eight Bay Area Korean tables.

Ohgane Korean BBQ — 3915 Broadway, Oakland. A Broadway pioneer of Bay Area Korean BBQ since 2006. Get the galbi.

Jong Ga House — 372 Grand Ave, Oakland. A Grand Avenue favorite for banchan and tofu stew since 2000. Order the soondubu.

Pyeong Chang Tofu House — 4701 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A cozy Temescal spot for bubbling soft tofu stew. Get a soondubu pot.

Dan Sung Sa — 2775 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A dim Korean pub covered in graffiti and old newspapers. Order the pojangmacha snacks.

Um Ma — 1220 9th Ave, SF. An Inner Sunset spot for homestyle Korean and galbi jjim. Get the galbi jjim.

Han Il Kwan — 1802 Balboa St, SF. A Richmond standby for Korean BBQ and stews. Get the bulgogi.

Manna — 845 Irving St, SF. A tiny Inner Sunset counter with a steady line. Get the dolsot bibimbap.

Jang Su Jang — 3561 El Camino Real, Santa Clara. A South Bay BBQ hall with premium cuts. Do a full BBQ spread.

Eight for Korean: Ohgane, Jong Ga House, Pyeong Chang Tofu House, Dan Sung Sa, Um Ma, Han Il Kwan, Manna, and Jang Su Jang. Where do you start?

The Bay Area does Indian food from a legendary Berkeley chaat counter to Michelin dining rooms in Palo Alto and Burlingame, among the deepest scenes in the country. Eight Bay Area Indian tables.

Vik's Chaat — 2390 4th St, Berkeley. The legendary chaat house for pani puri and cholle bhature. Get a plate of chaat.

Rooh — 333 Brannan St, SF. Modern Indian near the ballpark with creative small plates. Do the chef's picks.

Besharam — 1275 Minnesota St, SF. A Gujarati spot from a celebrated chef in Dogpatch. Order the thali.

Breads of India — 2448 Sacramento St, Berkeley. A daily changing North Indian menu. Try the daily thali.

Ajanta — 1888 Solano Ave, Berkeley. A regional Indian spot with a rotating monthly menu. Ask the special.

Fitoor — Santana Row, San Jose. A modern Indian restaurant in the former Amber India space on Santana Row, tandoor plates and cocktails. Order the butter chicken.

Ettan — 518 Bryant St, Palo Alto. A Michelin recognized modern Indian downtown. Book the tasting.

Rasa — 209 Park Rd, Burlingame. A Michelin starred South Indian on the Peninsula. Do the tasting.

Eight for Indian: Vik's Chaat, Rooh, Besharam, Breads of India, Ajanta, Fitoor, Ettan, and Rasa. Where do you start?

item.description: The Bay Area's sushi runs from a downtown omakase counter open since 1987 to a Sausalito landmark by the water, some of the best fish outside Tokyo. Eight
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Sushi

The Bay Area's sushi runs from a downtown omakase counter open since 1987 to a Sausalito landmark by the water, some of the best fish outside Tokyo. Eight Bay Area sushi counters.

Akiko's — 431 Bush St, SF. SF's pioneering omakase since 1987, pristine nigiri downtown. Sit at the bar.

Ju-Ni — 1335 Fulton St, SF. A counter omakase in a converted flat with chefs seat side. Book the counter.

Robin — 620 Gough St, SF. A playful Hayes Valley omakase with no printed menu. Trust the chef.

Sasaki — 2400 Harrison St, SF. A refined Mission omakase from a Kusakabe alum. Reserve ahead.

Kappou Gomi — 5524 Geary Blvd, SF. A Richmond spot for traditional Japanese, no rolls, just craft. Order the seasonal set.

Sushi Ran — 107 Caledonia St, Sausalito. A Marin sushi landmark for nearly forty years. Order the omakase.

Delage — 536 9th St, Oakland. An intimate Oakland Chinatown omakase counter. Book the seating.

Sushi Sam's Edomata — 218 E 3rd Ave, San Mateo. A Peninsula cult favorite for market fresh nigiri. Ask the daily specials.

Eight for sushi: Akiko's, Ju-Ni, Robin, Sasaki, Kappou Gomi, Sushi Ran, Delage, and Sushi Sam's. Where do you start?

item.title: Bay Area Thai
item.description: The Bay Area's Thai food earned a Michelin star near Union Square and runs deep from a Tenderloin institution to Lao and Thai kitchens across the East Bay.
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Thai

The Bay Area's Thai food earned a Michelin star near Union Square and runs deep from a Tenderloin institution to Lao and Thai kitchens across the East Bay. Eight Bay Area Thai tables.

Kin Khao — 55 Cyril Magnin St, SF. A Michelin starred Thai kitchen just off Union Square. Get the rabbit curry.

Nari — 1625 Post St, SF. A modern Thai room in Japantown from the Kin Khao chef. Do the tasting.

Lers Ros — 730 Larkin St, SF. A Tenderloin institution with a huge authentic menu. Order the crispy pork.

Farmhouse Kitchen Thai — 710 Florida St, SF. A festive Mission spot for northern Thai and cocktails. Get the khao soi.

Hawker Fare — 680 Valencia St, SF. A rice bowl spot rooted in Isan Lao and Thai flavors. Get a jasmine rice bowl.

Anchalee — 1094 Dwight Way, Berkeley. A Berkeley favorite for fresh, balanced Thai. Order the curry noodles.

Champa Garden — 2102 8th Ave, Oakland. An Oakland spot for Lao and Thai home cooking. Try the nam khao.

Amarin Thai — 156 Castro St, Mountain View. A downtown Mountain View Thai standby. Get the pad see ew.

Eight for Thai: Kin Khao, Nari, Lers Ros, Farmhouse Kitchen, Hawker Fare, Anchalee, Champa Garden, and Amarin. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco SF's Late Night Eats
item.description: When the bars close, San Francisco eats at a 1920s diner shaped like a rail car open till 4am and a Mission taqueria slinging burritos long past midnight.
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Late Night Eats

When the bars close, San Francisco eats at a 1920s diner shaped like a rail car open till 4am and a Mission taqueria slinging burritos long past midnight. Eight SF late night eats.

Grubstake — 1525 Pine St, SF. A diner in an old rail car serving burgers and Portuguese plates till the small hours. Get a burger at 2am.

El Farolito — 2779 Mission St, SF. The late night Mission taqueria for a foil wrapped super burrito. Order the al pastor.

Taqueria Cancun — 2288 Mission St, SF. A neon lit taqueria beloved for its late tacos. Get the carne asada.

Golden Boy Pizza — 542 Green St, SF. A North Beach counter slinging square Sicilian slices till late. Grab a clam and garlic square.

Yuet Lee — 1300 Stockton St, SF. A bright green Chinatown seafood spot for late salt and pepper squid. Order the squid.

Bob's Donuts — 1621 Polk St, SF. A 24 hour donut stop for a 3am apple fritter. Get the fritter warm.

Orphan Andy's — 3991 17th St, SF. A round the clock Castro diner with pancakes and shakes. Order a milkshake.

Pearl's Deluxe Burgers — 708 Post St, SF. A late night burger and shake window downtown. Get a Kobe burger.

Eight late night eats: Grubstake, El Farolito, Taqueria Cancun, Golden Boy, Yuet Lee, Bob's Donuts, Orphan Andy's, and Pearl's. Where do you start?

item.description: The Bay Area has flipped burgers the same way since 1958 at a San Leandro drive in, and the best patties run from a Berkeley college counter to a Palo Alto
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Burgers

The Bay Area has flipped burgers the same way since 1958 at a San Leandro drive in, and the best patties run from a Berkeley college counter to a Palo Alto soda fountain. Eight Bay Area burgers.

Val's Burgers — 75 Estudillo Ave, San Leandro. A family burger joint griddling since 1958, get the double Papa Burger. Order the Papa.

Super Duper Burgers — 721 Market St, SF. A local chain of griddled burgers and garlic fries. Add the garlic fries.

Causwells — 2346 Chestnut St, SF. A Marina spot with the smashed Americana double. Get the Americana.

WesBurger N More — 2240 Mission St, SF. A Mission smashburger counter with retro sauces. Order the classic.

Barney's Gourmet Hamburgers — 1591 Solano Ave, Berkeley. An East Bay burger institution with chili cheese fries. Get the curly fries.

Nation's Giant Hamburgers — 10630 San Pablo Ave, El Cerrito. A 24 hour Bay Area classic for burgers and pie. Add a slice of pie.

Palo Alto Creamery — 566 Emerson St, Palo Alto. A 1920s soda fountain for burgers and milkshakes. Get a burger and a shake.

Bongo Burger — 2154 Center St, Berkeley. A UC Berkeley burger and Persian joint since 1969. Get the classic burger.

Eight for burgers: Val's, Super Duper, Causwells, WesBurger, Barney's, Nation's, Palo Alto Creamery, and Bongo Burger. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco SF's Date Night Restaurants
item.description: San Francisco has done date night the same way for 30 years at a Nob Hill Italian temple, and the city still sets the mood from a Mission courtyard cinema
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Date Night Restaurants

San Francisco has done date night the same way for 30 years at a Nob Hill Italian temple, and the city still sets the mood from a Mission courtyard cinema to a bay view raw bar. Eight SF date night restaurants.

Acquerello — 1722 Sacramento St, SF. A Nob Hill Italian fine dining room for a milestone night. Do the tasting menu.

Gary Danko — 800 N Point St, SF. A polished tasting menu institution near the wharf. Build a plate flight.

Frances — 3870 17th St, SF. A warm Castro bistro with market driven California cooking. Get the bacon beignets.

Zuni Cafe — 1658 Market St, SF. The iconic wood oven room famous for a roast chicken for two. Order the chicken.

Foreign Cinema — 2534 Mission St, SF. A Mission courtyard restaurant screening films on the wall. Book the patio.

Aziza — 5800 Geary Blvd, SF. A Michelin Cal Moroccan room in the Richmond. Get the basteeya.

Octavia — 1701 Octavia St, SF. A refined neighborhood tasting spot in Pacific Heights. Sit at the counter.

Angler — 132 The Embarcadero, SF. A Michelin seafood room with a raw bar and bay view. Book a window at sunset.

Eight for date night: Acquerello, Gary Danko, Frances, Zuni Cafe, Foreign Cinema, Aziza, Octavia, and Angler. Where do you start?

item.description: The Bay Area's donut game runs from a 24 hour Polk Street counter open since 1960 to a Berkeley shop that put mochi donuts on the map. Eight Bay Area donut
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Donuts

The Bay Area's donut game runs from a 24 hour Polk Street counter open since 1960 to a Berkeley shop that put mochi donuts on the map. Eight Bay Area donut shops.

Bob's Donuts — 1621 Polk St, SF. A 24 hour SF counter since 1960, home of a giant apple fritter. Get the fritter warm.

Dynamo Donut — 2760 24th St, SF. A Mission shop of small batch flavors like maple bacon apple. Try the maple bacon.

Johnny Doughnuts — 1617 4th St, San Rafael. A Marin favorite of organic doughnuts and the cronut style Johnnut. Get a Johnnut.

Donut Savant — 6037 San Pablo Ave, Oakland. An Oakland shop of square cronuts and tiny bites. Grab a box of minis.

Colonial Donuts — 3318 Lakeshore Ave, Oakland. A 24 hour Lakeshore classic since the 1980s. Get a buttermilk bar at 2am.

King Pin Donuts — 2521 Durant Ave, Berkeley. A 24 hour Berkeley institution since 1939 for classic raised and cake donuts by the dozen. Order a dozen warm.

Third Culture Bakery — 2701 Eighth St, Berkeley. The Berkeley shop that popularized the mochi muffin and mochi donut. Get a mochi donut.

Psycho Donuts — 288 S 2nd St, San Jose. A wacky South Bay shop of over the top creations. Get something ridiculous.

Eight for donuts: Bob's, Dynamo, Johnny Doughnuts, Donut Savant, Colonial, King Pin, Third Culture, and Psycho Donuts. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco SF's Dessert Shops
item.description: San Francisco has a serious sweet tooth, from a bourbon and corn flake ice cream in the Mission to a chocolate factory that roasts its own beans on Valenci
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Dessert Shops

San Francisco has a serious sweet tooth, from a bourbon and corn flake ice cream in the Mission to a chocolate factory that roasts its own beans on Valencia Street. Eight SF dessert shops.

Bi-Rite Creamery — 3692 18th St, SF. The Mission ice cream counter with a line around the block for salted caramel. Get the salted caramel.

Humphry Slocombe — 2790A Harrison St, SF. The home of Secret Breakfast, bourbon ice cream with corn flakes. Order Secret Breakfast.

Craftsman and Wolves — 746 Valencia St, SF. A modern patisserie famous for the Rebel Within savory muffin. Get the Rebel Within.

Dandelion Chocolate — 740 Valencia St, SF. A bean to bar chocolate factory and cafe with s'mores. Do the hot chocolate flight.

Miette — 1 Ferry Building, SF. A dainty pastel patisserie of cakes and macarons. Take home a gingerbread cake.

Garden Creamery — 3566 20th St, SF. A Hawaiian inspired ice cream shop with mochi and vegan scoops. Try the ube.

Anthony's Cookies — 1417 Valencia St, SF. A tiny shop for warm, chewy, chocolate chip cookies. Get them by the box.

Schubert's Bakery — 521 Clement St, SF. A Richmond German bakery making cakes since 1911. Get a slice of Princess cake.

Eight for dessert: Bi-Rite, Humphry Slocombe, Craftsman and Wolves, Dandelion, Miette, Garden Creamery, Anthony's Cookies, and Schubert's. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco Sandwich Shops and Delis
item.description: Molinari has cured its own salami in San Francisco's North Beach since 1896, and the counter still draws a line out the door. Eight SF sandwich stops worth
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco Sandwich Shops and Delis

Molinari has cured its own salami in San Francisco's North Beach since 1896, and the counter still draws a line out the door. Eight SF sandwich stops worth the wait, from a dutch crunch corner store to a Tenderloin banh mi window.

Molinari Delicatessen — 373 Columbus Ave, San Francisco. North Beach's Italian deli has cured its own salami since 1896 and still slices it to order for sandwiches that need two hands. Come before the lunch rush or you will meet the whole neighborhood in line. @molinaridelicatessen

Lucca Delicatessen — 2120 Chestnut St, San Francisco. The Bosco family has run this Marina deli since 1929, rolling their own ravioli in back and stacking cold cuts up front. Grab a sandwich and a tub of fresh pasta for later. @luccadeli

Deli Board — 1058 Folsom St, San Francisco. This SoMa shop builds gloriously overstuffed sandwiches with house brined meats and names you have to decode off the board. Order online ahead, the midday line is real. @deliboardsf

Palm City Wines — 4055 Irving St, San Francisco. Out in the Outer Sunset, this corner spot stacks East Coast style hoagies next to a natural wine list. Grab a hoagie and a bottle and post up at the sidewalk tables. @palmcitywines

Wise Sons Jewish Delicatessen — 3150 24th St, San Francisco. The Mission's Jewish deli house cures its pastrami and piles it on rye, with matzo ball soup that tastes like somebody's grandmother made it. Save room, or take half home. @wisesons

Rhea's Deli and Market — 800 Valencia St, San Francisco. This corner market's spicy pork sandwich has a cult following, and you are barely a block from Dolores Park. Grab one wrapped to go and claim a patch of grass. @rheassandwiches

Roxie Food Center — 1901 San Jose Ave, San Francisco. A tiny Excelsior corner store hiding one of the city's best sandwiches: the Simon Special stacks turkey, pastrami, and cheddar on dutch crunch. Get there around noon and expect a line of regulars. @roxiefoodcenter

Saigon Sandwich — 560 Larkin St, San Francisco. In the Tenderloin's Little Saigon, this tiny window turns out some of the best banh mi in the city for a handful of dollars. Bring cash, order the combo, and do not expect a seat. @saigon.sandwich

Eight for San Francisco sandwiches: Molinari, Lucca, Deli Board, Palm City Wines, Wise Sons, Rhea's, Roxie, and Saigon Sandwich. Which counter gets your first stop?

item.title: San Francisco Peninsula Breweries and Taprooms
item.description: Everyone drives over the hill to Napa or the city for a good pint and skips the whole Peninsula. Their loss. Freewheel in Redwood City still hand pulls tra
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco Peninsula Breweries and Taprooms

Everyone drives over the hill to Napa or the city for a good pint and skips the whole Peninsula. Their loss. Freewheel in Redwood City still hand pulls traditional English cask ale off a real beer engine, the only brewery making it on the Peninsula. Eight Peninsula breweries and taprooms worth staying home for.

47 Hills Brewing Co — 137 S Linden Ave, South San Francisco. A dog friendly brewery and beer garden tucked into South City's industrial flats. That's exactly why the picnic tables never feel like a scene. Grab a flight, let the kids and the dog loose, and pretend you planned it. @47hillsbrewing

Fieldwork Brewing — 3030 S Delaware St, San Mateo. The Bay Meadows taproom rotates through a genuinely dizzying number of beers, so the hazy IPA you loved last week may already be gone. Come with a flexible plan and check the board before you commit. @drinkfieldwork

Alpha Acid Brewing — 121 Industrial Rd, Belmont. This tiny Belmont operation has brewed more than 500 recipes and often taps something new every week. That makes having a usual almost impossible. Ask what just went on, and trust whoever is pouring. @alphaacidbrewingco

Devil's Canyon Brewing — 935 Washington St, San Carlos. Every Friday afternoon this San Carlos mainstay throws open the taproom, barrel room, and beer garden for a family and pet friendly party with food trucks and live music. Show up before five if you want a table. @devilscanyon

Out of the Barrel — 555 El Camino Real, San Carlos. Not a brewery but a taproom with more than 30 rotating taps right at the San Carlos train plaza, so the whole table can disagree and everyone still wins. Kid and dog friendly, with empanadas to keep the peace. @outofthebarrelsancarlos

Freewheel Brewing — 3736 Florence St, Redwood City. Here is that English cask ale from up top, hand pulled off a beer engine and served at cellar temperature the way a proper pub would. Order the London Calling bitter, low in alcohol, high in flavor, built for a long afternoon. @freewheelbrew_redwoodcity

Hop Dogma Brewing — 270 Capistrano Rd, Half Moon Bay. Tucked into the Pillar Point Harbor row at Princeton, this small brewery pours hop forward ales a few steps from the fishing boats. Time it for late afternoon, walk the harbor first, then let the coast fog find you. @hopdogma

Half Moon Bay Brewing Co — 390 Capistrano Rd, Half Moon Bay. The waterfront original across from the harbor, all surf shack vibe and salt air, with its own beer beside sustainable local seafood. Post beach or post whale watching, this is where a coast day is meant to end. @hmbbrewingco

Eight for Peninsula beer: 47 Hills, Fieldwork, Alpha Acid, Devil's Canyon, Out of the Barrel, Freewheel, Hop Dogma, and Half Moon Bay Brewing. Which one is your Friday?
