item.title: San Francisco Bagels
item.description: Eight bagel shops in San Francisco, and not one of them is the chain by the freeway onramp. The best boil-and-bake in this city hides on side streets from
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco Bagels

Eight bagel shops in San Francisco, and not one of them is the chain by the freeway onramp. The best boil-and-bake in this city hides on side streets from NoPa to Bernal, and half the crowd still drives past them for the frozen stuff. Here is where the line is worth it.

Schlok's Bagels & Lox — 1263 Fell St, San Francisco. A takeout window in NoPa where the lox is cured and smoked in house, not pulled from a package. Get there before the sold-out sign goes up around 1:45, because it will. @schloksbagels

Boichik Bagels — 3665 Sacramento St, San Francisco. The Berkeley legend crossed the bridge and Presidio Heights got the payoff: a dense, chewy, Montreal-meets-New-York bagel that sells out most mornings. Open daily until 1:30 or gone. @boichikbagels

Wise Sons Jewish Delicatessen — 3150 24th St, San Francisco. The Mission deli that put SF on the modern Jewish-food map, and the bagels are kettle-boiled with malt syrup the old way. Order one with the pastrami and thank yourself later. @wisesons

The Bagel Bakery — 151 Townsend St, San Francisco. Boiling and brick-oven baking New York style since 1976, tucked near the ballpark in South Beach. It is the quiet old-school pick when everyone else is chasing the new sourdough spots. @the_bagel_bakery

The Laundromat — 3725 Balboa St, San Francisco. Bagels by morning, wood-fired pizza and natural wine by night, all in a converted Outer Richmond laundromat. Come for the everything bagel, stay because nobody wants to leave. @thelaundromatsf

Uncle Benny's Donut & Bagel — 2049 Irving St, San Francisco. The Inner Sunset spot that opens at 4am, so the fog-shift commuters and the after-hours crowd both get theirs warm. Donut in one hand, bagel in the other, no judgment. @unclebennysdonut

Bones Bagels — 741 Diamond St, San Francisco. Naturally leavened sourdough bagels in Noe Valley, crisp outside and tangy enough to eat plain from the bag. Open Thursday through Sunday. That's exactly when the line forms. @bonesbagels

Chicken Dog Bagels — 237 Cortland Ave, San Francisco. A one-man sourdough operation running out of Avedano's butcher shop in Bernal Heights, named after the owner's dog. Saturdays are for walk-up sandwiches, and the line down Cortland tells you it is worth it. @chicken_dog_bagels

The SF eight: Schlok's in NoPa, Boichik in Presidio Heights, Wise Sons in the Mission, The Bagel Bakery in South Beach, The Laundromat in the Richmond, Uncle Benny's in the Sunset, Bones in Noe Valley, Chicken Dog in Bernal. Which neighborhood gets your Sunday morning?

item.title: San Francisco South Bay Boba and Milk Tea
item.description: Eight South Bay boba stops worth the drive, all independent, zero chains in the mix. If your milk tea loyalty stops at the mall kiosk, this thread is your
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco South Bay Boba and Milk Tea

Eight South Bay boba stops worth the drive, all independent, zero chains in the mix. If your milk tea loyalty stops at the mall kiosk, this thread is your permission slip to wander a little. Save it before the next Friday craving hits.

Pekoe — 3276 S White Rd, San Jose. The split drinks are the move here, half one tea half another in the same cup, so you stop losing the flavor debate with yourself. Open past midnight most nights, which your 11pm sweet tooth will remember fondly. @pekoeteabar

Lacaphe — 740 Story Rd Ste 5, San Jose. A women-owned spot where the Vietnamese coffee does the heavy lifting and the boba tags along happily. Order the ca phe sua da with pearls and you understand why the Story Road line stays long. @lacaphe.sj

Tea Era — 20916 Homestead Rd Ste F, Cupertino. Slinging Taiwanese bubble tea since 2001, back when boba in Cupertino meant one or two places, not one per block. Get the classic milk tea and a side of popcorn chicken, the old-school combo that never needed fixing. @teaeracafe

Boba Oasis — 447 Great Mall Dr, Milpitas. Tucked in the Great Mall for when the outlet-shopping stamina runs out and you need something cold in hand. A tidy little independent counter that quietly outclasses the food-court usual suspects. @thebobaoasis

Boba Pup — 1080 Kiely Blvd, Santa Clara. They pour into collectible glass bottles, so your matcha comes with a keepsake you end up hoarding. Organic tea, real Vietnamese coffee, and a name that earns every dog lover walking past. @bobapupca

MoonTea — 513 S Pastoria Ave, Sunnyvale. Parked on the El Camino corner for a quick pull-off, with teas that lean aromatic and Chinese-tea forward instead of syrup-first. The kind of cup that reminds you tea was the point before the boba boom. @moontea.boba

ChaChaCha — 3623 Thornton Ave, Fremont. A woman-owned corner of Fremont doing pistachio matcha, Nutella milk tea, and croffles for the days one vice will not cover it. Come for the boba, leave planning your return around the 10 Won Ppang. @chachacha_fremont

Milk & Honey Cafe — 34265 Fremont Blvd, Fremont. A family Taiwanese kitchen where the boba shares a menu with hot pot and night-market bites, so the group with mixed cravings all wins. Closed Mondays, so plan the milk tea run for any other day. @milkandhoneyfremont

Eight independent South Bay boba stops, two in San Jose, two in Fremont, one each in Cupertino, Milpitas, Santa Clara, and Sunnyvale. Save this for the next craving and drop the independent shop that belongs on the list. The South Bay bench runs deep.

item.title: San Francisco Fremont Afghan Cuisine, Little Kabul
item.description: Eight stops through Fremont's Little Kabul, the largest Afghan community in the country, most of it packed into a few blocks of Fremont Blvd. Everyone race
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco Fremont Afghan Cuisine, Little Kabul

Eight stops through Fremont's Little Kabul, the largest Afghan community in the country, most of it packed into a few blocks of Fremont Blvd. Everyone races to one famous kabob counter and drives past the bakery, the market, and the family spots regulars quietly rotate through. Here is the run, from char-grilled classics to bread that comes out of the oven every few minutes.

De Afghanan Kabob House — 37405 Fremont Blvd, Fremont. The name everyone knows, and the char on the chicken and beef kabob is why. Grab the combo over a bed of rice, tear off some bolani, and understand fast why the line out front keeps moving all afternoon.

DeAfghanan Cuisine — 37395 Fremont Blvd, Fremont. Two doors down from the Kabob House and a separate kitchen after a family split, so locals argue which one wins. Come for the Qabili Palau, lamb buried under rice, raisins, and carrot, and pick your own side.

Maiwand Market — 37235 Fremont Blvd, Fremont. The grocery that anchors the strip, with a bakery firing long slippers of nan afghani through the whole day, plus a halal butcher and shelves of Afghan sweets. This is where the home cooks shop, so time a visit for warm bread.

Afghan Awasana Kabob — 37012 Towers Way, Fremont. Tucked off the main drag, which keeps it a regulars' secret. The draw is the kabob platter and a mantu that people drive across the bay for. Closed Mondays, so plan around it. @afghan_awasana_kabob

Fremont Kabob — 5379 Mowry Ave, Fremont. Off the Blvd near Mowry, open late once the Fremont Blvd spots have shut their kitchens. Order the chopan lamb chops, marinated and charbroiled, with a mound of rice and a side of their green sauce. @fremont.kabob

Authentic Afghan Kebab and Cuisine — 39965 Mission Blvd, Fremont. A newer family kitchen up on Mission that quietly built a following on its Qabuli Palau. Small room, big platters, and staff who steer first-timers toward the right kabob. Closed Wednesdays. @afghankebabandcuisine

Kabob Fusion — 41986 Fremont Blvd, Fremont. Further down the Blvd, where Afghan kabob meets Mediterranean and Turkish on one menu. Handy when the table cannot agree, one person gets the Afghan platter, another a wrap, and the zabiha halal grill covers both. @kabobfusionfremont

Maiwand Village — 5698 Thornton Ave, Newark. One town over, worth the short hop for the sit-down Afghan spread and a room built for big groups. Come with people, order the family-style platters and the aushak dumplings, and settle in. Closed Wednesdays.

That is the Little Kabul run: De Afghanan Kabob House, DeAfghanan Cuisine, Maiwand Market, Afghan Awasana, Fremont Kabob, Authentic Afghan Kebab, Kabob Fusion, and Maiwand Village in Newark. Kabob first or a warm sheet of nan first? Which block are you starting on?

item.title: Bay Area Napa and Sonoma Wine-country Hikes
item.description: Jack London bought a Sonoma ranch, called it Beauty Ranch, and spent his last years walking its hills above Glen Ellen. You can hike the same ground, past
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Napa and Sonoma Wine-country Hikes

Jack London bought a Sonoma ranch, called it Beauty Ranch, and spent his last years walking its hills above Glen Ellen. You can hike the same ground, past his cottage and the ruins of Wolf House, between the vineyards. Six Napa and Sonoma wine-country hikes.

Jack London Mountain and Quarry Loop — Jack London State Historic Park, Glen Ellen. 3.2 miles, 551 feet of gain, moderate, loop, 4.7 stars. Past the cottage and the Wolf House ruins on Beauty Ranch. @castateparks

Fern Lake via Mountain and Vineyard Trail — Jack London State Historic Park, Glen Ellen. 5.2 miles, 902 feet, moderate, out and back, 4.7 stars. Up through the vineyard to a hidden lake.

Canyon and Pony Gate Loop — Sugarloaf Ridge State Park, Kenwood. 2.2 miles, 652 feet, moderate, loop, 4.7 stars. A short creek loop past a seasonal waterfall.

Rough Go and Canyon Loop — Trione-Annadel State Park, Santa Rosa. 6.0 miles, 643 feet, moderate, loop, 4.7 stars. Rolling oak and meadow out to Lake Ilsanjo.

Lake Ilsanjo via Spring Creek — Trione-Annadel State Park, Santa Rosa. 4.6 miles, 498 feet, moderate, out and back, 4.6 stars. The straight shot to the lake and back.

Spring Lake Loop — Spring Lake Regional Park, Santa Rosa. 2.1 miles, 36 feet, easy, loop, 4.7 stars. A flat, stroller-friendly lap around the water.

Six in wine country: Jack London two ways, Sugarloaf, Annadel two ways, and Spring Lake. Which one earns the tasting after?

item.title: Bay Area Wine Country Hikes
item.description: Jack London poured the fortune from Call of the Wild into a Sonoma ranch, and the ruins of his dream mansion still sit in the hills you can hike today. Eig
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Wine Country Hikes

Jack London poured the fortune from Call of the Wild into a Sonoma ranch, and the ruins of his dream mansion still sit in the hills you can hike today. Eight wine country hikes.

Jack London State Historic Park — Glen Ellen. Trails past the author's cottage, the Wolf House ruins, and a lake, 3.2 miles up Jack London Mountain. Walk the writer's ranch.

Sugarloaf Ridge State Park — Kenwood. The Bald Mountain climb, 5.6 miles to a summit with a view from the Sierra to the sea on a clear day. The big Sonoma view.

Bothe-Napa Valley State Park — Calistoga. The Ritchey Canyon and Redwood trails wind through the easternmost coast redwoods, cool and green. The shady canyon walk.

Trione-Annadel State Park — Santa Rosa. Rolling oak and meadow trails to Lake Ilsanjo, wildflowers in spring and great for a trail run. The rolling ramble.

Mount St Helena at Robert Louis Stevenson Park — Calistoga. The climb to Napa's highest point, where Stevenson honeymooned, a big 10 mile day. The summit challenge.

Sugarloaf's Canyon and Pony Gate Loop — Kenwood. A shorter loop past a seasonal waterfall on Sonoma Creek, best after winter rain. The easy waterfall walk.

Skyline Wilderness Park — Napa. A Napa park with a climb to Lake Marie past an old rock dam, quiet oak trails on the valley's edge. The Napa local hike.

Oat Hill Mine Trail — Calistoga. A historic wagon road climbing out of Calistoga with valley views and old mining relics. The history underfoot hike.

Eight in wine country: Jack London, Sugarloaf Ridge, Bothe-Napa, Annadel, Mount St Helena, the Pony Gate waterfall, Skyline Wilderness, and the Oat Hill Mine Trail. Which trail first?

item.title: Bay Area A Day Trip to Sacramento
item.description: Sacramento sprang up as the Gold Rush boomtown where the Sacramento and American rivers meet, and today you can bike 32 miles of riverside trail from its o
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area A Day Trip to Sacramento

Sacramento sprang up as the Gold Rush boomtown where the Sacramento and American rivers meet, and today you can bike 32 miles of riverside trail from its old waterfront. Eight Sacramento day trip stops.

Old Sacramento — Sacramento. A 28 acre waterfront district of Gold Rush era buildings, wooden sidewalks, and a paddlewheeler on the river. Walk the boardwalk.

California State Railroad Museum — Old Sacramento. One of the great railroad museums, gleaming locomotives and a seasonal steam train ride. See the big engines.

State Capitol and Park — Sacramento. The neoclassical Capitol from 1869 set in a park of trees gathered from around the world. Tour the dome and the grounds.

Tower Bridge — Sacramento. The bright gold vertical lift bridge over the Sacramento River, best at sunset from the promenade. Walk out at golden hour.

American River Parkway — Sacramento. A 32 mile paved trail along the river from Old Sacramento to Folsom, bikes, herons, and swimming holes. Rent a bike and ride.

Crocker Art Museum — 216 O St. The oldest public art museum in the West, a Victorian mansion joined to a modern wing, free Thursday evenings. Wander the galleries.

Midtown Sacramento — Sacramento. A grid of leafy streets with cafes, murals, and farm to fork restaurants, the city's hip heart. Grab coffee and wander.

Sutter's Fort — Sacramento. The reconstructed 1839 fort where the settlement began, costumed history in the middle of the city. Step into the past.

Eight in Sacramento: Old Sacramento, the Railroad Museum, the Capitol, Tower Bridge, the American River Parkway, the Crocker, Midtown, and Sutter's Fort. Where do you start?

item.title: Bay Area Livermore Valley Wine Country
item.description: The Bay Area has grown wine grapes in Livermore Valley since 1883, and readers pushed us past First Street to the vineyards themselves. Eight Livermore win
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Livermore Valley Wine Country

The Bay Area has grown wine grapes in Livermore Valley since 1883, and readers pushed us past First Street to the vineyards themselves. Eight Livermore wineries.

Longevity Wines — 2271 S Vasco Rd, Livermore. A family run, minority owned winery with a barn themed tasting room. Taste the reds. A @belivellc add.

Darcie Kent Vineyards — 7000 Tesla Rd, Livermore. A women owned estate on Tesla Road pouring award winning varietals. Sit on the terrace. A @belivellc add.

Wood Family Vineyards — 2407 Research Dr, Livermore. A small production favorite readers named beside Longevity and Darcie. Try the red. A @belivellc add.

Concannon Vineyard — 4590 Tesla Rd, Livermore. A Tesla Road winery founded in 1883, among the state's oldest. Walk the historic grounds.

Retzlaff Vineyards — 1356 S Livermore Ave, Livermore. An organic estate winery celebrating 50 years of pouring. Picnic on the lawn.

McGrail Vineyards — 5600 Greenville Rd, Livermore. A hilltop winery with big Cabernet and a valley view. Toast at the overlook.

Las Positas Vineyards — 1828 Wetmore Rd, Livermore. A winery with food, live music, and wide lawns. Bring a group for the afternoon.

Page Mill Winery — 1960 S Livermore Ave, Livermore. A low key winery open late on select Thursday evenings. Catch a Thursday pour.

Eight Livermore wineries: Longevity, Darcie Kent, Wood Family, Concannon, Retzlaff, McGrail, Las Positas, and Page Mill. Which one first?
